WALKSTAND BACKDRAWNRULE

How people move through the club

Club Tier Stage 13, expanded. Five people who run a club, twenty-six journeys and the navigation, walked on real screens, then stood back from. This page holds the walk, what cuts across it, what is not navigation, the stage ladder, the end state drawn, and your asks.

26 + the navjourneys: five per person (owner, club admin, league admin, registrar, treasurer) and the president’s view
255 findings20 High · 98 Medium · 137 Low, each linked to its station
508 captureseach with its measurements: height in screens, words above the fold, where the main action sits, targets under size

How it was walked

  • On real screens, by walk helpers driving a browser as each person: a local production build of the current code, never the shared dev server (ruling R2).
  • On the review’s own fixture clubs: "Fresh Hollow Minor Ball" (just bought, invites pending) for the first days, and "Harbourtown Minor Ball" (a year of history, every program running) for the rest. Journeys that change data ran on their own copy.
  • Computer at 1440 × 900; phone at 390 × 844 for phone tasks and the whole nav.
  • Each journey stopped at the send: nothing that emails a person or charges a card was pressed (R3: walking to the send is enough; the review is about how the app moves each person through the job).
  • Judged on the thirteen points in the plan: first-time ease, flow, the whole experience, layout, text, sizing, where am I, is this mine, dead ends, one name per thing, feedback, effort, and the hand-off.

How to read the findings

  • A flag is a finding: red High, amber Medium, grey Low. Click one to read it and jump to its station. The red number on a tab ("5H") counts that tab’s High findings.
  • A helper’s finding is a lead. Every High was checked by me against its capture or the code before it went on this page: ✓ confirmed ✎ corrected ↪ re-framed or routed ■ already built. Mediums and Lows without a mark are the walker’s read.
  • Checking found one new High the walks missed (removing a member who is also a parent deletes their family sign-in), corrected three (the dome draft is a builder defect, not the fixture; Withdraw does say it emails; two outstanding totals are a labelling problem, not a money error), and settled four questions the walks raised (below and on tab 10).

What was not seen

  • Anything past a send: the coach’s side after the dome schedule is sent (O2), the public site after house league publishes (L2: publishing teams emails families).
  • The door between the admin and the Coaches Portal: no owner or admin in the fixture coaches a team.
  • A cancelled club, a person in two clubs, a published house league division.
  • One stop-rule slip: a helper pressed a single-row Approve twice on its own copy. Both families’ addresses are on a reserved test domain that can’t deliver, and dev sends no email. Nothing reached anyone. It is also finding F-R2-4: that button emails with no word and no confirm.

Settled while checking

  • Buying Club: ruled self-serve with a 90-day trial (2026-09-25), but no plan builds the club’s door. A release gap, routed (Ask 22).
  • Receipts: not on a club ledger line, not on a coach’s request, and not in any plan. A new item.
  • The dome draft’s lopsided split: the schedule builder, not the fixture. Fix now.
  • The tournament’s "payments aren’t tracked here": the fixture set no fees; the line is the not-set-up fallback. A crossing question that keeps two standing rulings (Ask 16).
  • The double bill: real. Nothing joins the schedule’s draft bill to the treasurer’s billing (Ask 15).

The president’s view · can Morgan see the whole club at a glance?

You added this after the walks: "this summary level reporting and views will be key to sell to club presidents who have to deal with so much information." The walk asked ten questions from the owner’s first screen. The product answers the club’s finances and this week in one click, permits per permit, and leaves the rest for the president to assemble. The Overview answers none of the ten directly, though most answers sit one screen below it with nothing pointing there.

What it needs is mostly surfacing, not building

  1. The Accounting Overview ("Where the club stands") is the best summary screen in the product, and the best on a phone. The Calendar answers this week. Families › Show already counts who owes, missing forms and who can’t be reached. The permit window gives held, booked and unused.
  2. So the Overview gains a club band built from those (Ask 2, drawn whole-screen on tab 12), and a Permits door (Ask 1). Both are Stage 13 navigation.
  3. "Where is each coach with their budget" is answered, as you re-framed it: each team’s standing with the club (allocated, collected, outstanding, overdue, held by the team) is on Accounting › Teams, two clicks away. The band surfaces it. The coach’s own budget and spending stay the team’s (D1, not re-opened).
  4. Three answers don’t exist anywhere: free time across permits by week, players across programs with last season beside them, and a whole-club board one-pager. A fourth, which tournaments each team entered, is the one question still open (Ask 5). That is product work, and you decided its frame the same day (Business Decisions Log, 2026-11-06, "Club’s headline promise to a president: one place that pulls the whole club together"): it follows the Club release, League Plus carries it too, and it never looks into a coach’s own books. It gets its own plan (Ask 3), coordinated with Stage 13 so the Overview isn’t built twice (Ask 4).

The walk predates your rulings of 2026-11-06. Where it reads question 2 as each team’s own budget against spending (its Station 2 and shape question 1), read it as you re-framed it: each team’s standing with the club, which is answered. D1 stays.

Station 0The Overview — where a president starts

  • What they see: "THIS MORNING" (4 count cards: tryout applications 0, payment requests 3, installments due 12 · 7 overdue, assistant coaches 0), then "YOUR PROGRAMS": six door cards (Rep teams, House league, Accounting, Families, Public site, Tournaments) with a one-line description each, then a quiet Organization row and "Setup: 4 of 5 steps done".
  • My read: the Overview is a menu of doors, not a summary. Only the four "This morning" cards carry a figure, and all four are *things waiting on you*. No cash, no owed, no players, no "this week", no permits, no tournaments. Six of the ten questions are answered one screen below it, and the Overview does not even hint at where (the Accounting card lists its tab names, not its numbers). For the owner's stated purpose (a president wants it synthesized with minimal effort) this is the biggest single gap, and it is a product gap, not a navigation one: the facts exist and are good (see Q4: the Accounting Overview is exactly the right grain), they just do not appear on the first screen.
  • Findings: · High · The club Overview carries no club-level figure (no cash, owed, players, this week, what is at risk); it is six door cards and four "waiting" counts. Evidence . Direction: decide what the president's one-glance band is (Q4's three figures, players, this week, at-risk) and put it above the doors. · Low · "Installments due 12 · in the next 14 days · 7 overdue" does not say whether the 7 are inside the 12. Evidence . · (Reuse of : the quiet Organization row still has stray spaces before the colon and commas.)

Station 1Q1 What permits, dates and times do we have available (held vs booked vs free, all permits, a date range)?

  • What they see and do: nothing on the Overview or the sidebar says "permits". The route I would guess: Organization (sidebar or the quiet Overview row) → Venue library (a list of venues with "Booked by this season") → the Permits switch. That is Overview → Organization → Venue library → Permits: 3 clicks, 3 page changes. A first-timer lands on Venues, not Permits, and "Lakeshore Dome · Nothing booked" is the only hint a permit is involved.
  • The Permits list is good: one row per permit, all permits together, grouped IN USE NOW / STARTS LATER, with dates, hours a week, used % and "0 of 450 h", and cost (). Open a permit and the window gives HELD 80 h · BOOKED 7.5 h · UNUSED 72.5 h, split by facility with the teams on it, and "Hand out this time in a schedule" (). That is held / booked / unused, as asked.
  • What it cannot do: the figures are for the whole permit period (7 weeks, 25 Sundays), not a date range; there is no "what is free on Sunday Jan 10, across everything"; the Calendar shows what is booked, never what is held and free (its Venue filter offers only venues with bookings, so Lakeshore Dome is not even listed, ). Held-but-unbooked time is shown only as a total per permit. The list's "Used" column also shows only %, so the president opens three windows to read the hours.
  • Verdict: PARTLY ANSWERED. Per permit, yes (held/booked/unused, all permits in one list). By date range / "when is it free": not answerable. Hidden: the door sits under Organization, a heading that otherwise means members and settings.
  • Phone: reachable (More → Venue library → Permits, 3 taps); the list reflows to one line per permit (); glanceable.
  • Findings: · Med · Permits (held / booked / unused) are two levels down under Organization › Venue library and nothing on Overview or Calendar points to them; a president hunting "what time do we have" has no word to follow. Evidence vs . Direction: a Permits door at the same level as Calendar/Schedules, or a held-and-used line on the Overview. · Med · No date-range view of held vs booked vs free across permits; used time is per permit period only. Evidence O6-04/05/06. Direction: product gap (a free-time view by week), not navigation.

Station 2Q2 Where is each coach / rep team with their budget (budgeted vs spent, dues collected, what they owe the club)?

  • What they see and do: the natural start is Rep teams ("coaches") or Accounting. Both work. Accounting › Teams (Overview → Accounting → Teams tab: 2 clicks) is a one-screen table of all 8 teams: Allocated · Collected · Outstanding (with overdue in red) · Requests · Cash on hand held by the team, grouped Junior/Senior with a total row (). The Rep teams list also carries an Outstanding column per team, plus roster and documents "9 of 12" (). Click a team and its account shows what it owes, next due, paid to the team, a statement ().
  • What the team owes the club: ANSWERED, at a glance, and on a phone ( reads "13U AAA · Holding up a payout · $3,300.00 owed · + $600.00 overdue from 2025–26"). Strong.
  • A team's own budget (budgeted vs spent on the coach's side): NOT ANSWERABLE FROM THE CLUB, by deliberate boundary. The only coach-side figure the club gets is one number, "Held by the team" cash on hand, in a locked column with the footnote "The coaches' own books, never part of the club's figures" (; lib/club-money-words.ts:390, :581). The team page states the rule on screen: "What the club sees … The team's cash on hand (one figure; never its families' payments or its other spending)", with "The coach's alone: Attendance, Lineups, Awards, Player development, Opponents and scouting, Practice plans" (; lib/club-money-words.ts:604, lib/help-content/rep-teams.tsx:21). The coach's budget and dues exist in that coach's Coaches Portal (Money · Budget · Player dues; I confirmed the page exists as navj-club-coach-15aaa, ), one portal at a time. The team page's lists name neither the coach's budget nor the coach's tournament list in either column, so this is a boundary by silence, not a stated ruling. Present as a question for the owner (Shape question 1).
  • Consistency: the same team shows two totals. 13U AAA is $3,900 outstanding on Rep teams and $3,300 (plus a "+ $600.00 overdue from 2025–26" line) on Accounting › Teams; the Teams total is $9,750 and the Overview's "Owed by the teams" is $10,950. Explainable (prior-year carry-over) but a president holding two screens will see two different numbers.
  • Findings: · Med · One team, two outstanding totals on two screens ($3,900 Rep teams vs $3,300 Accounting › Teams; $9,750 vs $10,950 overall) and "Collected" differs again ($1,800 Teams tab, $2,400 Overview "from the teams, on allocations", $2,750 BvA "From the teams"); I could not reconcile them from the screens. Evidence , , , . Direction: one definition, or a one-line "includes 2025–26" on each. · Low · Phone Rep teams drops the Outstanding and Documents columns the desktop list has (); the money for a team is one tap deeper than on desktop. Direction: add the overdue chip to the phone row.

Station 3Q3 Which tournaments is each rep team signed up for (across teams)?

  • What they see and do: the club's "Tournaments" door lands inside *the club's own* tournament (Harbourtown Invitational), a dashboard of 4 teams registered (), and a list of tournaments this club hosts (). Nothing there says which tournaments the club's rep teams enter elsewhere. The rep team page has no tournaments section (); the Rep teams list has none (); the Calendar shows only the hosted tournament's days (a "Tournament · 15U · 4 games" row, ).
  • Where the data is: each team's own Coaches Portal › Tournaments (/coaches/teams/{id}/tournaments: "Coming up · Nov 16–18 · Harbourtown Invitational 2026 · ACCEPTED", ; the page is built to hold the team's registrations in any organization's tournament, tournament-history). The club admin cannot see it.
  • Verdict: NOT ANSWERABLE FROM THE CLUB. The data exists, per team, in the coach's portal (fixture shows only the hosted tournament for 15U AAA; I could not see an away entry). The shipped boundary text does not list it either way (see Q2). Whether the club should see its teams' tournament entries is the owner's call; it is also the kind of item a president would actually ask in a board meeting ("who is going to Cooperstown?").
  • Findings: · High (product gap, not navigation) · The president cannot see which tournaments any rep team has entered; the only "tournaments" the club shows are the ones it hosts. Evidence , , . Direction: owner decision whether a "Tournaments" shelf on the club's team page / a cross-team line on Rep teams is allowed (Shape question 2).

Station 4Q4 Where are we as an organization financially?

  • What they see and do: Overview → Accounting (1 click, 1 page change; it is also the third phone tab with the waiting badge). "WHERE THE CLUB STANDS · TODAY, NOV 6": Cash on hand $2,870 · Owed by the teams $10,950 ($3,450 overdue) · Waiting on you $920, then what is still open from last year, "2026–27 against the budget" (planned vs so far, net, headroom $40,490), the teams, and "The club's books": 4 ledgers (General, the tournament, two house leagues) with balances. 1.8 screens on desktop, fits one phone screen well and every number reads as a sentence (). This is the best summary-level screen in the product: it is what a president means by "synthesized". Budget vs. Actual () adds the four-figure band (Collected, Spent, Off-plan, Cash on hand) and the line-by-line, which includes house league registration fees and tournaments.

(b) "Owed by us" is only "Waiting on you $920" (coach requests); I found no line for committed or unpaid costs such as the $27,000 dome permit, which the permit window files "On the budget" but the Overview does not show as to-pay. (c) The tournament's money is one ledger line, not a figure in the band.
  • Verdict: ANSWERED (1 click, at a glance, phone-safe) for cash, owed by the teams, owed to the teams, budget vs actual; PARTLY for house league receivable and for what the club itself owes.
  • Findings: · Med · The financial summary leaves out the house league receivable ($1,740 still owing, 12 players) and any "committed, not yet paid" cost, so "owed to us" and "owed by us" are each short. Station 5Q5 The winter dome schedule and the house league schedule together, or easily one to the other (a week, and the season)

  • What they see and do:
    • A week: ANSWERED. Calendar (1 click) is the one place that puts the club's practices from the club schedules, house league games and the club's tournament in one list, in time order, with a program filter, venue filter, a clash flag, and List / Week / Month (, week view : Tue Nov 17 shows 14U AA and 11U AA practices beside the tournament; Thu Nov 19 shows 13U AAA practice and the house league game "Reds vs Blues"). A week is exactly the grain a president wants. Phone: a Calendar tab, 1 tap ().
    • The season: ASSEMBLED BY HAND. The dome schedule lives under Schedules (a club schedule, opened from a permit, per O2); the house league schedule lives under House league › a season › Schedule, one division at a time (: it opens on U9 Rookie and shows one game). The bridge between them is a sentence on the season page ("The club hasn't given this season any time yet. It gives it in the club's Schedules") and the "House league's time" window, which on navj-club just says "The club hasn't given house league any time yet" (). On a club with both built, the owner can click through from the time window to the club schedule (per the nav census), but there is no single season view with the dome and the house league side by side.
    • What I could not see: the fixture has the dome permit (Lakeshore Dome, 450 h held, 0 booked) and no built club schedule, so I could not see the dome's Sunday slots, their teams, or how they sit next to house league time. The Calendar Venue filter lists Kinsmen Park, Lions Park and "Places the club doesn't own" (no Lakeshore Dome) precisely because nothing is booked there ().
  • Verdict: ANSWERED for a week (Calendar); ASSEMBLED BY HAND for the season (two tools, two lists). Remember Schedules is also owner/admin only; a league admin sees house league's half of the calendar but cannot open Schedules.
  • Findings: · Med · No season-level view puts the club's schedules and a house league season together: the dome season is under Schedules, the house league season is under its own season > Schedule, and the only link between them is a sentence and a window. Evidence , , . Direction: let the Calendar month stand in as the "season view" (it already shows counts per day, ) and link to it from both. · Low · The Calendar's month cells say "4 bookings · 1 clash" but never which programs; you must switch to Week to see the dome beside house league. The journey as a whole

  • Where a first-timer gets stuck: the Overview. It is a sheet of doors, so the president must know that *Accounting* is the financial summary, *Calendar* is "this week", *Organization › Venue library › Permits* holds the permits, *Families › Show* holds the risk counts and *Past seasons* holds last year. None of that is stated on the first screen.
  • The good news is large: the building blocks are very good and mostly one click from the Overview (Accounting Overview, Accounting › Teams, Calendar, Families filter counts, the permit windows, the board report, a very clean phone). The synthesis the owner wants is mostly *surfacing*, not building.
  • Top 3: (the Overview shows doors, not the club), + (at-risk and the player count are assembled across screens), (a team's tournaments are not visible to the club).

Shape questions for the owner

  • 1. Should the club see a team's own budget (budgeted vs spent), not just its one cash figure? — Not yet, ask first. Today the club sees one figure ("Held by the team") and the screens call the rest "the coaches' own books, never part of the club's figures" (lib/club-money-words.ts:390/581/604; team page panel ). I found a stated rule for cash and the lists, but none for the coach's budget or the coach's tournament list, so this is a boundary by silence. If you want presidents to see "budget vs spent per team", the honest product is a rolled-up line the coach consents to (or a club-run team budget), not reading the coach's book. It also touches what a coach expects to be private.
  • 2. May the club see which tournaments its rep teams have entered? — Keep the boundary open and decide: this one reads like a *record* (a team entering a tournament), not an instrument, and a president asks it constantly. Recommendation: Reshape toward yes, as a read-only "Tournaments" line on the club's team page and one cross-team list; it rides on whether coaches can enter away tournaments privately.
  • 3. Should the club Overview lead with a one-glance band (cash, owed, players, this week, at-risk) above the doors? — Reshape, yes. It is the same data the Accounting Overview, Calendar and Families filter already hold; the Overview becomes the board summary, and 's printable page falls out of it.
  • 4. Is "this week" meant to be on the Overview, or only the Calendar? — Reshape: put "next event" on the Overview and on an empty Calendar week.
  • 5. One club "Players" figure with last season beside it (house league + rep)? — Reshape/Not yet: the data joins in Stage 14, and the Families "Not back this season" count is an early version. Decide whether the number is children or families.
  • 6. Where should Permits live? — Reshape: it sits under Organization › Venue library behind a venue list; a president thinks of permits as "time we have", beside Calendar and Schedules.

Owner · Morgan Ellis, President, who bought the plan

The owner's everyday screen works: "This morning" is the right first look, and the crossings into a tournament and back are one click each on a computer. The owner's hard jobs work too, once found. The winter dome and house league's time both start with a guess (permits live in Organization › Venue library › a Permits switch) and both end by handing work to someone the product doesn't tell. The first day traps the owner on the setup checklist at every sign-in, and buying Club has no door yet.

Keep: "This morning" on the OverviewKeep: Permit → schedule pre-fill ("Hand out this time in a schedule")Keep: The coach’s arrival in the Coaches Portal (O4)Keep: One click into a tournament and one back

Five journeys, one at a time. Each station: the captures (click to open at full size, with the measurements), what the walker saw and did, their read, and the findings. A flag opens the finding; ✓ means the parent reopened the capture or the code.

Stripe is never reached.

The journey as a whole

  • Where a first-timer gets stuck: at the very first step — a president cannot buy Club from the pricing page (/2). After that the product is easy to learn: the checklist is good, the Overview and the rail are quick to read, and the hand-off to the board is honest (the checklist notices who joined). What quietly goes wrong is that the checklist never lets go () and that Overview's top card says nothing is waiting on a club with four open invitations and zero setup done.
  • Hand-offs: owner → board: the invite form (wrong default, missing roles, generic email) and a checklist that does report "have joined". Nothing tells the owner when the league admin or registrar joined (the bell stays empty).
  • What it says about the nav: the checklist is a chrome-less mini-product that the rest of the app has no door back into (); permits are named nowhere an owner would look; "Also on your plan" mislabels a program the club is about to run.
  • Top 3: 1) Club cannot be bought from the Club button. 2) owner lands on the checklist at every sign-in (confirmed live, twice). 3) + /18: permits hidden in Venue library; invite form's wrong default and the missing house league roles.

Shape questions for the owner

  • Does the checklist end? (Mark setup done on "Go to Overview" / after step 5, and keep "Setup n of 5" on Overview until then.) — Reshape: recommend yes; it is a one-line fix and it removes a page every owner passes through at every login. Rides on: the owner's first impression every day.
  • Should permits have a named door (rail row "Permits" under Organization, or a checklist step "Add your venues and permits")? — Reshape: recommend a checklist step plus the Overview text, not a new rail row; the owner's tab-in-Venue-library opinion is borne out in walking (4 clicks, named nowhere). Rides on: O2/O3 journeys.
  • While Club is consultative, should the pricing page ever show a "Start your Club trial" button? — Reshape: recommend one source of truth for "can Club be bought here" feeding the pricing card, /for-clubs and the plan door; when Club opens, give it its own buy path rather than the tournament door. Rides on: launch.
  • Does the invite form offer league admin / registrar before a season exists? — Reshape: recommend show-disabled with the reason.

O2 · The winter dome, end to end — Owner (desktop; coaches on desktop + phone)

Started at: the club Overview of navj-club-2 (owner navj-club-2-owner), as an owner who has "rented the dome" and now wants a schedule, a send-out and a bill · Finished? With help. Permit, schedule, fair-share bill and the send screen were all reached and read. I did NOT press "Send to 6 coaches" or "Final now" (hard stop), so the coach's side AFTER the send is unverified (see Station 6). Two things I did press on my own copy: "Save as a draft" and "Add the bill to the schedule" (neither emails anyone) · Effort (natural route, permit to send screen): about 15 clicks, 7 page/dialog changes: Organization, Venue library, Permits tab, the permit row, "Hand out this time in a schedule", fix the practices select (the default fails), Generate drafts, Save, View menu to Fair shares, Bill the teams, Add the bill, Send, "See Taylor's email".

Fixture notes: the copy has no club schedule (as briefed), the permit has the seed's note text ("Seeded for the Stage 10a walks…") in Notes and no document. Today in the fixture is Nov 6 2026, so the Oct 4 permit is already "In use now" with 0% used. 8 rep teams show; 16U AA is "between seasons" and drops out of the schedule form ("1 team has no season running").

Station 1Where does an owner go to enter or check the dome permit?

  • What they see and do: the owner's first instinct for "the dome" is Schedules (it sits right under Calendar). Schedules says only "A schedule hands the club's time to its teams: a dome's winter nights, a town's field permit. Start one with New schedule." It never says that a permit comes first or where permits live. There is no Permits row anywhere in the sidebar. The owner has to guess Organization (the chevron that holds Members, Audit log, Settings, Venue library, PDF settings), then Venue library, whose first view is the venue list (Kinsmen, Lakeshore Dome, Lions, Westfield), and only then notice the quiet "Permits" toggle next to "Venues". The Organization hub tile says "The club's venues and their facilities, booked by every program" and never mentions permits. Venue-list page copy also does not mention permits.
  • My read: First-time ease: poor, a hunt (the owner's own opinion "permits are hidden in venues" is borne out on the screen). Where am I: fine once there (the permit list is a proper page: issuer and reference, where, dates, hours a week, used, cost). Is this mine: ok. One name per thing: the left nav calls it Organization, the page "Venue library", the tab "Permits", the dialog "Permit"; the thing the owner calls "the dome contract" is the "permit" with Lakeshore Dome as ISSUER, which a dome rental is, but the word "permit" is a town-field word. A dome booking is a "rental".
  • Findings: · Med · permits are reachable only via Organization > Venue library > Permits toggle; nothing on Schedules, Overview or the Organization hub tile mentions them · evidence O2-01 (Schedules empty state), O2-03 (hub tile), O2-05 · direction: say "permits" on the Schedules empty state and the hub tile with a link, or give permits their own door. · Low · a dome is a rental, not a permit; the vocabulary is the town-field word · O2-05/06.

Station 2Open the permit: does it capture a real dome contract?

  • What they see and do: the permit window shows Issuer (Lakeshore Dome), Reference W26-118, For (The club), dates with "6 months · 25 Sundays", Document ("No document"; Upload the permit (PDF) in edit), Notes, The time (Fields 1-6, Sun 8:00-11:00 a.m., 450 h held, date off Dec 27 with a reason), Cost ($27,000, $72/hour full field, $36 half fields, the arithmetic spelled out), the budget line it pays from ("Dome time - winter dome", with "Open the line"), and Use (held, booked, unused). Renew for next year is there. This is a strong screen.
  • Captured: dates, weekly slots, fields, hours, cost per hour per field, the reference, the document upload, dates off, the budget line, renewal. Missing for a real dome contract: how and when the CLUB pays the dome (deposit, instalments, due dates, a payment schedule to the dome) - the budget line just says "No date yet"; a contact (name, phone, email at the dome); cancellation/refund terms and the weather or closure clause beyond one "date off"; a deposit; GST/HST on the contract (the cost is one number, no tax line); an expiry or option-to-renew date. The only free text is Notes.
  • My read: Does the flow make sense: yes. Text: good, the cost explanation answers the question where it arises. Effort: opening is one click. Editing is a pencil that becomes a tick (no visible Save label; first-timer may not know the tick saves).
  • Findings: · Med · no field for what the club owes the dome and when (payment schedule/deposit), and no contact or terms; the owner cannot record "we pay $9,000 on Oct 1, $9,000 on Jan 1" anywhere on the permit · O2-07 · direction: a small "How we pay for it" block on the permit that feeds the budget line's dates (today "No date yet"). · Low · the edit mode saves with an unlabelled tick icon · O2-07 top right.

Station 3Hand the permit out as a winter schedule (permit to scheduler)

  • What they see and do: from the permit, "Hand out this time in a schedule >" opens the New schedule dialog already filled in ("Filled in: Lakeshore Dome, Fields 1-6, Oct 4 - Mar 28, Sundays 8:00-11:00 a.m., Dec 27 off"), name too, with a live "25 Sundays · 6 fields · 18 slots a Sunday · 450 slots" and "450 slots for 7 teams. Nothing left open." That hand-off is excellent. From the Schedules page the same dialog has a Permit dropdown with the same fill. House league is unticked, 7 rep teams ticked with "193/257" and per-team slot counts. The owner presses Generate drafts.
  • The default settings then fail. The form said "Nothing left open", but with the default "Practices per team, per day: 1 practice" the three drafts score 64/100 and say "7 teams short: 14U AA by 40, 15U AA by 54, 15U AAA by 59, 9U AA by 62, 11U AA by 62, 12U AA by 63 and 13U AAA by 63 ... 403 slots left open", handing out 47 of 450 (14U AA gets 25, 13U AAA gets 1). Switching the rule "Never on a team's game day" off changed nothing; "Moved around" changed nothing; only raising the practices select to "3 practices" gave 99/100 and 450 of 450. Nothing on the form tells the owner that the practice-a-day select is what limits the result; the only clue is the small grey line under the select. A first-timer would think the product is broken or that the club's rep teams cannot use the dome.
  • And even at 99/100 the result does not match the form's own promise "Each team keeps its facility and start time week to week, so families can plan around it": on the saved grid each team lands on a different field and hour every Sunday, and 14U AA's review email lists 18 separate rules ("Sundays, 8:00-9:00 a.m. · Field 2, Oct 4 - Mar 21, not on 22 of those weeks").
  • 65 slots is also 54 hours: every rep team gets about 2.5 hours of dome EVERY Sunday for 25 weeks. A real club would say "one hour a week each" (the "A set number a week" split exists but is not the default and the form never nudges to it). The fixture's 450 slots / 7 teams is the cause, so this is partly fixture arithmetic, but the product's "Nothing left open" line pushes toward filling everything.
  • My read: Flow: permit to schedule is the best hand-off in the journey. Text: the Rules ("2 on", collapsed) and the select hint are too quiet for what they do. Feedback: the draft scoring is clear and the shortfall warning is honest; but there is no "why". Sizing: a two-screen dialog on a desktop is okay.
  • Findings: · High · the default "1 practice per team, per day" turns a 450-slot dome into a 47-slot draft scored 64/100 and the form never warns, while its own footer says "Nothing left open" · O2-08 footer vs O2-09 (47 of 450) vs O2-13 (450 of 450 at 3/day) · direction: derive the per-day default from slots divided by teams, or flag it on the form before Generate. · Med · "The same each week" promise is not kept in the saved schedule (teams change field and hour every week) and the coach email lists up to 18 pattern lines per team · O2-14 grid, O2-22 email · direction: either keep the promise or stop making it. · Low · the owner is given no reason when a rule (game day) removes slots; turning it off made no difference, which is confusing · O2-10/11.

Station 4The schedule page: read it, adjust it, find the bill

  • What they see and do: the page opens as a grid (DRAFT chip) with four tiles: HANDED OUT 450 of 450, THE BILL $27,000.00, SHORT 0, CLASHES 0. The grid is a week-by-week matrix. Tools holds Settings, Regenerate unlocked slots, Lock these Sundays, Clear, Send log, Delete this draft. The bill is NOT where the tile suggests. "THE BILL $27,000.00" is not clickable (I clicked it; nothing opened). It is the dome's price to the club, not the teams' bills. The per-team split lives under the "View" pill (Grid / By team / By group / Fair shares) which a first-timer reads as another way to look at the schedule, not as billing. In Fair shares, a quiet link at the top right "Bill the teams >" opens the billing dialog.
  • The billing dialog is good: Bill from (the permit's budget line, "$27,000.00 planned, $27,000.00 left"), Bill the teams for (the whole price, or a part when the club covers some), Split ("By the time each team got", each field at the permit's price so half fields count half), Payments (One payment / Monthly / Every two months / Dates I choose), per-team rows with "43 full + 22 half · 54 h", payments Oct 1 / Dec 1 / Feb 1 totalling $9,720 / $8,640 / $8,640, and "Matches the permit's $27,000.00: nothing left for the club to cover." Plus plain text: "Nothing is billed until you finalize. Then each team's share arrives on its Money > Club tab with its 3 payments, filed under Dome Time where the team's budget has it." This answers the owner's billing question inside the schedule, without Accounting.
  • Defects in it: the first payment date defaults to Oct 1, 2026, which is already past on the fixture's today (Nov 6) and BEFORE the permit even starts (Oct 4), so the first installment is overdue the moment it is finalized; the dialog does not warn. The primary button says "Add the bill to the schedule" while the heading and the link say "Bill the teams" and the explanation says "finalize" - three verbs for one act. After pressing it the link becomes "The bill - 3 payments" and a toast says "The bill rides with the schedule until you finalize"; nothing on the page says what "finalize" is (it is on the Send dialog as "Final now").
  • My read: Layout: the main action (Send) is above the fold. One name per thing: "THE BILL" tile (the club's cost) vs "Bill the teams" vs "The bill - 3 payments" (the teams' cost) - the same word for two amounts that happen to match here. Where am I: the page does not link back to the permit it came from (the subtitle "Lakeshore Dome · Fields 1-6 · Sundays..." is plain text). What comes next: the page does not tell the owner "Bill the teams, then Send"; a first-timer who ignores a quiet link will Send without a bill.
  • Findings: · Med · the team split (the bill) hides behind View > Fair shares and a small top-right link; the tile named "THE BILL" does nothing when clicked · O2-14, O2-16 · direction: make the tile open Fair shares or put "Bill the teams" next to Send. · Med · billing default first payment is Oct 1, before the permit's own start and already past; no warning · O2-19 · direction: default to the first future 1st of the month on or after the permit start/finalize date. · Low · three verbs ("Bill the teams", "Add the bill to the schedule", "finalize"/"Final now") for one act · O2-19, O2-21. · Low · schedule header does not link to its permit; the permit window says '"Winter dome 2026-27" hands this time out, so the permit stays' but also still shows "Hand out this time in a schedule >" and neither links to the existing schedule · O2-14, O2-29.

Station 5"Send it out to the teams" (STOPPED before sending)

  • What they see and do: the Send dialog opens with "Send: For review first / Final now". "For review first": coaches see their slots and their bill and reply by a date (default Fri, Nov 13); "Nothing is booked or billed yet. You finalize when you're ready, whether or not every team has replied." It lists WHO REVIEWS · 5 TEAMS, 6 COACHES each with the team, coaches' names, "25 Sundays · $3,888.00 in 3 payments"; then a warning card "Nobody to send to · 2 teams": 9U AA has an invitation nobody accepted; 12U AA has no head coach; their slots "wait for Finalize; nobody is emailed about them. Name or chase its coach from its Coaches page." Buttons: "See Taylor Brooks' email", Cancel, "Send to 6 coaches" (not pressed). Each coach gets one email with the slots AND the bill, and a reply comes to the owner. The preview is clear: To, Subject "Winter dome 2026-27: 14U AA's slots and bill, for review", then 18 pattern lines, then "The bill: $3,888.00 in 3 payments... Oct 1 · $1,368.00, Dec 1 · $1,188.00, Feb 1 · $1,332.00", a link "Review it on 14U AA's Overview", and "Reply by Fri, Nov 13: Looks good, or Ask for a change."
  • My read: Hand-off: genuinely good. The send screen shows the money, the people, what is NOT sent and why, and a true preview. Text: the preview is the weak part: 18 lines of "not on 22 of those weeks" is unreadable for a coach (a table of dates or a calendar link would do); the bill's Oct 1 date is in the past. Is this mine: the owner can only fix a missing head coach by leaving the dialog and going to the team's Coaches page; there is no link in the warning.
  • Findings: · Med · the coach email lists slots as up to 18 "…, not on N of those weeks" rule lines per team (65 slots) - not readable on a phone · O2-22 · direction: a compact week-by-week list or a link to the page, lead with first practice and the total hours. · Low · the "Nobody to send to" card names the fix ("Name or chase its coach from its Coaches page") but does not link to it · O2-21. · Low · the email promises "Review it on 14U AA's Overview" - see Station 6: I could not verify the coach can.

Station 6The receiving end: rep coaches in the Coaches Portal

Coaches walked: navj-club-2-coach-15aaa (15U AAA, desktop) and navj-club-2-coach-13aaa (13U AAA, phone).

  • What they see: before the send, nothing about the dome. The 15U AAA Overview shows Next game, "This week: Nothing else", Money "Not set up". The coach Schedule lists only the Harbourtown Invitational games. Money > Club ("What the club has billed us") lists Diamond fees 2026, Fall ball diamond fees 2026 and Permit share 2025-26 - no dome bill. 13U AAA on the phone is the same: landing, Schedule, and Money > Club (one overdue installment for the Permit share, no dome). The draft schedule, its slots and its bill are invisible to coaches until the owner presses Send (as designed: "Nothing reaches a team until you send it"). I did not press Send, so I could not see: the review banner the email promises on the coach's Overview, the "Looks good / Ask for a change" reply, the post-finalize Schedule entries, or the Club-tab dome row with its 3 payments. That half of O2 stays unverified; it needs one more walk where Send is allowed on a throwaway copy.
  • The coach side does tell the truth about money in general: the Club tab on phone is a clean list ("Still to pay the club $3,900.00, 5 installments, 1 overdue"), and it fits a 390px screen (2.4 screens, no small targets worth noting).
  • Findings: · Med · until the owner sends, a coach has no way to know a dome schedule or a bill is coming; there is no "the club is preparing a winter dome schedule" note (acceptable as designed, but it means the first the coach hears of a $3,888 bill is an email) · O2-23/24/25 · direction: owner's call; keep. · High, UNVERIFIED · the entire coach end (review banner, reply, Schedule, Club tab) is untested because the only way to get there is the Send button · Station 5 · direction: re-walk on a copy where Send is permitted.

Station 7The way between tasks (what told the owner what came next)

FromToHow the owner got thereDid the screen say what comes next?
OverviewPermitOrganization > Venue library > Permits toggle > rowNo: nothing leads there
PermitSchedule"Hand out this time in a schedule >" in the permit windowYes - and the form is pre-filled

The journey as a whole

  • Where a first-timer gets stuck: (1) finding the permit; (2) the default schedule that gives 47 of 450 slots; (3) finding where the teams are billed (a menu item called "Fair shares" plus a small link).
  • The hand-offs: permit to schedule is excellent, schedule to send is excellent (the send dialog is the best screen in the journey), schedule to bill is hidden, bill to Accounting is a promise in a sentence, and the way back to the permit is missing in both directions.
  • What it says about the nav: the work is three tasks in three corners (Organization for the permit, Schedules for the schedule and its bill, Accounting for the money record and later reminders) joined by links in only one direction.
  • Top 3 issues: (High, default 1 practice a day wrecks the draft with no warning), (Med, the bill is behind View > Fair shares; the BILL tile is inert), (Med, permits hidden).

Shape questions for the owner

  • Should the permit have its own door (a Permits row under Organization, or on Schedules as the first step "1. Permit, 2. Schedule, 3. Bill, 4. Send")? — Reshape - recommend a visible permit link on the Schedules page and Overview; riding on it: every first dome/field season starts here.
  • Should a dome rental be a different thing from a town-field permit (payment schedule, contact, deposit)? — Reshape - recommend adding "how we pay for it" to the permit so the treasurer sees the club's outgoing dates; riding on it: the Budget line says "No date yet".
  • Should "Fair shares" and "Bill the teams" move to the toolbar next to Send, as the second step before sending? — Reshape - recommend yes; riding on it: owners sending a schedule without a bill.
  • Should the default practices-per-day be derived from the slot count? — Reshape - recommend yes; riding on it: a first-time owner reading a 64/100 result as a product failure.

O3 · Give house league its share of the club's time — Club owner (desktop), copy navj-club-3

Started at: the owner's Overview (/navj-club-3/admin), because that is where sign-in lands · Finished? Yes, but only by finding the permit-to-schedule door myself. The mixed rep-plus-house-league path could not be finished (Send emails 6 rep coaches, a hard stop), so I finished with a house-league-only schedule · Effort: 8 clicks, 4 page changes via the permit (Organization, Venue library, Permits tab, permit window, hand-out dialog); about 3 clicks via Schedules > New schedule if the owner already knows to pick the permit.

Station 1Find the permit that fits the season

  • What they see and do: Overview has a House league card ("Seasons, registrations, the draft, schedules and standings") but nothing about time or permits. The natural guess is Schedules (rail, third item). That page says "No schedules yet ... a dome's winter nights, a town's field permit. Start one with New schedule." Permits live in Organization > Venue library > Permits tab, which a first-timer has to know.
  • Permit choice: Winter dome 2026-27 (Lakeshore Dome, Oct 4 2026 - Mar 28 2027, Sundays 8-11 a.m., 6 fields, 450 h). It is the only one that covers Nov 27 - Feb 4. Fall diamonds ends Dec 17; Summer fields starts May 2027. The Permits list gives dates and "0 of 450 h used" in one row, so choosing is easy once you are there.
  • My read: First-time ease Med (two routes, neither signposted from House league). The permit window ends with the link "Hand out this time in a schedule >", small text at the foot of a tall window. The window never says who the time is for beyond "The club"; "house league" does not appear.
  • Findings:
    • · Med · Nothing on the Overview House league card or the season says "the club has not given this season time yet", so the owner has no prompt to go to permits. Evidence: . Direction: a quiet "no time given yet" line on the House league card while a season runs.
    • · Low · The route from a permit to a schedule is a small text link at the foot of a tall window (). Direction: a button.

Station 2"Hand out this time in a schedule" (New schedule, step 1)

  • What they see and do: The permit fills name, venue, fields, dates, days, hours and the Dec 27 closure. "Who, and how much" lists every rep team ticked, and "House league - Its league admins divide its share" under Programs, unticked. Ticking it with "Evenly" gives house league 56 of 450 slots (one team's share, 12.5%), though it has 4 divisions and about 9 teams. "By percentage" and "A set number a week" need typing into a column of 11 fields. I used a set number (HL 8 a week, rep groups 1 a week each) and got drafts scored 99/100.
  • "Send" on the saved draft opens a dialog whose WHO IS TOLD lists 6 rep coaches and says "Sending makes 175 slots real bookings." House league and its league admins are not in it. I stopped there (it emails coaches). , O3-14-send captured text only in the log.
  • Alternative that works: untick everything except House league. The footer becomes "House league gets 18 hours a week across 6 facilities, Oct 4, 2026 - Mar 28, 2027. Its league admins can divide it right away." and the button is Give it to house league. One click saved and sent it with no confirmation; the header reads "sent Nov 6 by Morgan Ellis", 450 of 450 handed out. This is the clearest screen in the chain.
  • My read: Flow makes sense for house-league-only, muddier for a mixed split. Defaults favour the rep side (all rep teams ticked, HL not). "Evenly" quietly under-gives house league. Text is good ("its league admins divide its share"), but the collapsed "1 team has no season running" is unexplained.
  • Findings:
    • · Med · "Evenly" counts house league as one team (56 of 450); a first-timer who ticks HL and generates hands it 12.5% of the dome. Evidence: . Direction: show HL's share explicitly or default to a percentage.
    • · Med · The mixed schedule's Send dialog lists only rep coaches; it never says whether the league admin is told, although its own copy says league admins divide HL's share "after you send". Direction: add a House league line to WHO IS TOLD.
    • · Low · "Give it to house league" saves and sends in one click with no summary of what the league admin will see. Direction: say "the league admin is not emailed".
    • · Low · The league admin's later dialogs show the permit's range ("Oct 4, 2026 - Mar 28, 2027 - 36 game slots in all"); the 36 only matches the season's real dates (Nov 29 - Jan 31), so the range text misleads.

Station 3Does the league admin learn about it?

  • What happens: No. The bell for navj-club-3-leagueadmin says "No notifications yet" on Unread and on All. No email is promised anywhere (dev cannot deliver, but neither the Give-it footer nor the Send dialog names one). Their landing is the Seasons list. The season Overview then says "The club hasn't given this season any time yet. An owner or an admin gives it, in Schedules." right after the club did, and the Schedule page says "U9 Rookie has no time from the club yet." Only the time window shows the gift: "Given by the club in Winter dome 2026-27 ... Not given yet, 18 hours a week" where "not given yet" now means "not yet given to a division". The Overview note cleared only after the time was divided.
  • Findings:
    • · High · The league admin is never told that time was given, and the screens they see say the opposite until they divide it. Evidence: note, bell empty. Direction: a bell item and email to the season's league admins on give, and change the note to "The club has given 18 h a week; divide it among divisions".

The journey as a whole

  • Where a first-timer gets stuck: finding permits; the Evenly default; Send meaning something different for house-league-only (no one emailed) and mixed schedules (coaches emailed).
  • Hand-off: the club gives the time and leaves no trace for the receiver.
  • Top 3: , , .

Shape questions for the owner

  • Should giving time to house league tell the league admin (bell plus email)? — Keep the one-click give, add the notice. Everything downstream depends on the league admin noticing.
  • Should "Evenly" count house league as one team? — Reshape: make HL's share explicit. Rides on how much of the dome HL ends up with.
  • Should the House league season Overview carry a door for the owner to give time (today only a line pointing at Schedules)? — Keep; add the Overview prompt.

O4 · A new rep season — Owner (desktop; the coach's arrival on desktop + phone)

Started at: /navj-club-4/admin (Overview; the owner lands there on sign-in, setup line "4 of 5 steps done" in the footer) · Finished? Yes, to the stop (invite not sent). The coach's first step was followed with the seeded accept link for the 9U AA head coach. Effort: to roll ONE team forward and name a head coach: Overview → Rep teams (1) → team row (2) → Start next season (3) → radio (4) → Start the 2027 Season (5) → sidebar "Coaches" (6, page change) → Invite a coach (7) → email + role → Send (8, not pressed). About 8 clicks and 4 page changes per team, repeated per team. 8 teams = 8 passes; there is no way to do the club's teams together.

Copy changes made (navj-club-4 only): 12U AA rolled to the 2027 Season; 9U AA's pending head coach (Dana Whitaker) accepted.

Station 1Where does the owner start?

  • What they see and do: Overview has four "This morning" tiles (tryouts, payment requests, installments, assistant coaches) and a "Your programs" grid. Nothing mentions next year or a new season. The owner goes Rep teams. The table has a Season column that reads "2027 · LIVE" on 14U AA and 9U AA, "2026 · LIVE" on five teams, and "2025 · CLOSED" on 16U AA. No Head coach on 12U AA shows a red tag; 9U AA shows "INVITED" plus an address.
  • My read:
    • First-time ease: Med. Nothing on the club pages says "start the new year here". The owner has to guess "Rep teams, then open each team". The only hint is a button inside each team.
    • Where am I (season): the club has no season of its own. Each team is on its own year, so "2027 rep season" is not a thing the club can see, ask about or finish. After one team rolls, the table shows a mixed list with no marker for who has not moved.
    • Is this mine: "Past seasons" and "Bring in a coach's team" sit in the Rep teams sidebar group beside Teams. Neither is the first move of a new year.
  • Findings: · Med · No club-level "new season" door and no bulk move; every team is its own dialog. Evidence: O4-02 (mixed 2025/2026/2027 chips), 8 teams. Direction: a "Next season" strip on Rep teams that lists teams still on last year and rolls them from one place (or at least a filter and a count).

Station 2Roll a team forward

  • What they see and do: The team page header carries "Close the season" and a bright "Start next season". The dialog explains what comes with the team (budget, fee plan, opening balance, each returning player's history), what starts fresh, that waivers need re-signing, and warns "12U AA's 2026 books aren't settled: 3 installments ($1,350.00) still owed" with "You can still start". Two radios: same players moving up an age group ("12U becomes 13U") or a new group, same age group. Choosing "moving up" and confirming gives the banner "The 2027 Season has started. 12U AA's coaches have been told."
  • My read:
    • Flow makes sense: yes. The dialog is the best screen in this journey. It names what carries over and warns without blocking.
    • Text: dense but it is where the question arises. The "Choose what the team is doing." hint is only visible once you scroll to the dialog foot; the primary button is greyed with no reason shown until then.
    • Feedback: wrong in two ways. (a) Right after confirming, the page still reads "2026 SEASON · LIVE", division "12U", "Birth years for the 2026 season" and two seasons in the list; it only shows 2027 after a reload (O4-10 vs O4-11). (b) The banner says "12U AA's coaches have been told" on a team with 0 coaches.
    • Naming: "12U becomes 13U" changes the Division field only. The team is still named "12U AA" with public address navj-club-4/teams/12u-aa, and the club already has a "13U AAA". Nothing in the dialog says the name will not follow.
    • Name per thing: "Start next season" (button), "Start the 2027 Season?" (dialog), "Start the 2026 Season" (closed-team page), "Season" as a word on 2025/2026/2027 chips. Close enough, but "Close the season" sits beside "Start next season", which also closes it. The dialog does say so, the buttons do not.
  • Findings: · Med · Moving up an age group does not rename the team or its public address, and the dialog does not say so. Evidence: O4-09 text; O4-11 Team details shows Name "12U AA", Division "13U", address 12u-aa. Direction: say it in the dialog and offer a new name in the same step. · Med · The team page is stale after the rollover until reload. Evidence: O4-10 shows the success banner over "2026 SEASON · LIVE". Direction: refresh the page data on success. · Low · "Coaches have been told" appears on a team with no coaches. Evidence: O4-10. Direction: drop the clause when there are none.

Station 3Name a head coach

  • What they see and do: Two routes to the same page: the Coaches card on the team page ("No coaches yet — Invite the head coach from the team's Coaches page") and the sidebar "Coaches". My first click on "Coaches" landed on Assistant coaches (the club oversight page) because the sidebar also lists "Assistant coaches" under Rep teams; the page reads "Head coaches invite and set their own staff". The team Coaches page has a red band "12U AA has no head coach. The team's row on Rep teams stays red until someone accepts." and one "Invite a coach" button (twice). The dialog asks Their email and "Who are they?" (Head coach — runs the team / Assistant coach — coaches the team). It says "They get an email with a link that works for 7 days. Their access starts when they accept." Stopped before Send. Captured address navj-club-4-newhead12@dev.local.
  • My read:
    • Is this mine: yes, and the "what the club sees" panel on the team page (Yours to run / The coach's, and you can read it / The coach's alone) is a good answer to "what will the coach own". It is a lot of text for a screen the owner opens to do one thing.
    • One name: "Coaches" (team), "Assistant coaches" (club), "Staff" (what the coach calls it, see station 4), "Invite a coach". A first-timer will confuse the first two. The dialog's "Who are they?" is a role question wearing a person question's label.
    • No name field: the invite takes an email only, so the owner's list shows the raw address until the coach accepts (see station 5).
  • Findings: · Med · "Coaches" and "Assistant coaches" are side-by-side sidebar rows with different jobs, and the nearest-looking one is the wrong one. Evidence: my own wrong click; O4-12 first attempt landed on /rep-teams/assistant-coaches. Direction: rename the club page "Staff approvals" or fold it into the team page. · Low · "Who are they?" should read "Role". Evidence: O4-13.

Station 4The coach's first step into the Coaches Portal

  • What they see and do: The accept page says "Coach 9U AA as head coach. Morgan Ellis invited you to Harbourtown Minor Ball (navj-club-4). Set a password to finish." First name, last name, password, one button. After joining they land directly on their team's Overview (/navj-club-4/coaches/teams/{id}), greeted "Welcome to 9U AA, Dana — Harbourtown Minor Ball named you head coach on Nov 6." Below it a second card: "This is your team's portal … Show me around / Add players instead". A "Season setup 0/5" pill, a glance row (Roster 0, Next up Nothing, Money Not set up…). The first cold paint shows "…" placeholders (O4-15) and fills in a few seconds later.
  • My read:
    • The hand-off works. The coach does not need to find anything; they are put on their team, by name, with the club named and the role. Better than most journeys in this review.
    • Where am I: header says "9U AA · Harbourtown Minor Ball (navj-club-4) · 2027 Season". Good. The accept page does not say "Coaches Portal" or what it is, and it is a bare public-site frame (Home / Scores / Pricing nav) that offers a "Get started" menu to someone who is already invited.
    • Layout: two welcome cards stack (the club's "named you head coach" and the portal's "this is your team's portal"), pushing the glance tiles down. The "DRAFT" tag beside "Overview" is unexplained to a person who just arrived.
    • Phone: the install-app banner covers the bottom of the first screen (O4-18) over the tiles and the bar. Roster is empty ("Your roster is empty … Paste your roster / Add one player"), which is right: the club has not placed players.
    • Text: the coach sees "2027 Season" with 0 players and no practices. Nothing tells them who to ask or that the club (not they) will open tryouts on the next season ("Tryouts: Closed — Opens on the next season" is on the owner's side only).
  • Findings: · Low · Two welcome cards back to back, and an unexplained "DRAFT" chip on a coach's first screen. Evidence: O4-16. Direction: one welcome; drop or explain the chip. · Low · Install banner covers the first phone screen on arrival. Evidence: O4-18. Direction: hold it until the coach's second visit.

Station 5Back to the owner: does the club hear it?

  • What they see and do: The owner's bell shows 1: "9U AA has its head coach — navj-club-4-newcoach@dev.local accepted your …". The Rep teams row now reads "Dana Whitaker" with "NO PLAYERS" still on it.
  • My read: hand-off closes the loop, a good moment. The notice shows the email, not the name the coach just typed. The owner's next step (get players onto 9U AA) is not offered; the row only says NO PLAYERS.
  • Findings: · Low · The "has its head coach" notice names the email, not the person. Evidence: O4-21. Direction: use the display name once it exists.

The journey as a whole

  • Where a first-timer gets stuck: before the first click ("where do I start the new year?") and at the second team, when they realise it is a dialog per team.
  • The hand-off to the coach is good. The hand-off to the owner after accept is good. The weak part is the middle: the club has no season of its own.
  • Top 3: (1) no club-level new-season door or bulk roll (Med). (2) age-group move leaves name and public address as they were (Med). (3) "Coaches" vs "Assistant coaches" (Med).

Shape questions for the owner

  • Should the club have a rep season of its own (a "2027" the club opens and teams join), or stay per-team? — Reshape (smaller): a "Next season" strip on Rep teams listing teams still on last year with a roll-all-selected action. Rides on: the closed-season ruling that a season is per team; the strip would not change that, only where the owner starts it.
  • Should "moving up" offer to rename the team and its address? — Keep the rule, Reshape the dialog.

Yes, with one detour: the tournament's money is found in the club's books, but not from the tournament and not by the route the screens suggest · Effort: Overview → open the tournament: 1 click, 1 page change. Station 1Open the tournament

  • What they see and do: The Overview card and the sidebar both say "Tournaments". One click goes straight into "Harbourtown Invitational 2026", landing on its Dashboard — not a list. The whole frame changes: the left rail swaps to TOURNAMENT with the name, then OPERATIONS (Dashboard, Teams, Schedule, Results, Check-in, Staff kit, Communications), SETUP (Event settings, Venues & facilities, Divisions, Rules & resources, Public site), ADMIN (collapsed). The first row is "Club overview" with a layout icon. The page title is the tournament; the club name is a small line above it ("HARBOURTOWN MINOR BALL (NAVJ-CLUB-4) · NOV 16–18, 2026 · OPEN").
  • My read:
    • First-time ease: fine for a club with one tournament; there is no "which one?" screen. With two tournaments (I created a second), the phone's tournament sheet still opened the older one, "Harbourtown Invitational 2026 - Live", although the new draft is listed first; which one the club door opens when there are two was not pinned down.
    • Where am I: clear on desktop. The top strip still says "ADMIN AREA", and the tournament name sits on the rail and the title. The way back ("Club overview") is the first row of the rail and always visible.
    • One name per thing: the club's door "Tournaments" means "go into one"; inside the tournament, ADMIN → "Tournaments" means "the list of all of them, and New tournament". Same word, two jobs, 1 and 3 levels deep (O5-04).
    • Layout: dashboard cards lead with registration health, a payments card, coaches, messages, schedule. Compact and honest.
  • Findings: · Med · The club's "Tournaments" opens one event's dashboard; the list and "New tournament" are hidden under ADMIN → Tournaments inside it, behind a collapsed group. Evidence: O5-01 (lands on Dashboard), O5-03 (ADMIN collapsed), O5-04 (the real list). Direction: let the club door open a list when the club has the list's job to do (new, reuse), or add a "New tournament" next to the switcher.

Station 2Create a new tournament

  • What they see and do: ADMIN → Tournaments → "New tournament" (primary, above fold y). A window offers "Reuse a previous tournament setup — best for annual tournaments" (lists Harbourtown Invitational 2026) or "Start blank tournament". Blank opens a 3-step window with a live phone preview of the public page on the right: 1 name, dates, style (Round robin + playoffs / Bracket only / Exhibition) and public link; 2 divisions (chips U9–U19, Open, Competitive, Recreational, "you can skip this"); 3 venues, picked from the club's venue library (Kinsmen Park, Lakeshore Dome, Lions Park, Westfield School) or a one-off venue. Then a "Ready to create" review ("Create the draft") and the new tournament's dashboard: DRAFT, "Before you activate 3 of 3 done", "The rest, when you're ready 1 of 6", an Activate button.
  • My read:
    • Flow makes sense: yes. Short, skippable, a preview that makes the stakes concrete. Picking venues from the club's library is a real club-to-tournament crossing and it works.
    • Text: "Reuse a previous tournament setup" is the first thing on offer, which is right for an annual event, but the old tournament's money setup is not described as part of what is reused.
    • Dates can be typed (2027-06-12); a first-timer will use the picker.
    • Feedback: lands on the draft dashboard with a readiness list. Good.
    • "Step 3 of 3" is followed by a fourth screen (the review). Minor.
    • After creation the rail's tournament name switches to the new one with the old as a second line (the switcher), no confirmation of which one the club door will open next.
  • Findings: · Low · "Step 3 of 3" is followed by a review step. Evidence: O5-10 then the "Ready to create" screen. Direction: "Step 4 of 4" or fold the review into step 3.

Station 3Into tournament admin and back to the club — desktop and phone

  • Doors, by device:
    • Desktop in: Overview card "Tournaments", or sidebar "Tournaments" (Programs group). Out: rail row "Club overview" (first row, 1 click). In: 1 click. Out: 1 click.
    • Phone in: bottom bar has Overview · Calendar · Rep teams · Accounting · More; Tournaments is not on the bar. It is under More → Programs → "Tournaments" (2 taps). Out: More → "Club overview" (first row, 2 taps). The bar swaps to Dashboard · Teams · Schedule · Messages · More inside a tournament, the badge "1" rides More.
    • More inside the tournament lists Notifications, "CURRENT TOURNAMENT" with a picker ("Harbourtown Invitational 2026 - Live"), Operations (Results, Check-in, Staff kit), Setup (5 rows), ADMIN (Settings & access, Tournaments), then the person's own rows (Account, Home, Plan & billing, Help…).
  • My read:
    • Where am I: on the phone the header shows the date, status and tournament name; the club name is not visible, nor "Admin area". Only the More sheet's first row says where the club is. The globe at top right opens the public site, unlabelled.
    • One name per thing: "Club overview" inside, "Overview" outside (the census's N6). "Dashboard" is both the tournament's first page and the bar's first tab. "Messages" on the phone bar vs "Communications" in the desktop rail (Operations); the phone More sheet does not list it at all, so the bar is the only phone door. "Public site" appears three times in the tournament frame (Setup → Public site, the top-right pill, the phone globe) and is the tournament's page, not the club's.
    • Sizing: phone tap targets fine (0 small targets). The More sheet scrolls past the fold; Sign out and Plan & billing are cut off at the bottom of the first screen.
  • Findings: · Med · On the phone, Tournaments is two taps deep and the way back is two taps; the phone header never says which club it is. Evidence: O5-23, O5-24 (no club name), O5-25 ("Club overview" first in sheet). Direction: show the club name (or a back arrow) in the tournament header on phone. · Low · "Messages" (phone bar) vs "Communications" (desktop rail) for the same page. Evidence: O5-24 bar, O5-03 rail. Direction: one word.

Station 4Find the tournament's money in the club's books

  • What they see and do — start inside the tournament, as an owner who wants "what did this make?": 1. The dashboard's Payments card says "Not set up — payments aren't tracked here". Clicking it opens Event settings → "Fees & payments" (Fee model Tournament-wide, deposit and total empty, "Filed under: Hosted tournament · Harbourtown Invitational 2026 — Entry fees and costs filed under this category appear together in By activity"). It is a fee-setup form and does not mention the club's books or the money already there. 2. The club's books do hold it. Club overview → Accounting. The Overview tab ends with "The club's books — 4 ledgers": the club's General ledger, Harbourtown Invitational 2026 (TOURNAMENT) $1,940.00, the two house league seasons. Clicking it opens the Ledger tab on that book. It opens on "This month" (Nov 1–30) and reads Balance $1,940.00 / "Nothing on this book in this window". After Date → All time: Oct 17 "Team registrations — three visiting teams · E-Transfer" Registration revenue $1,440.00 in; Oct 29 "From … General · Tournament float · transfer" $500.00 in. Nothing out. 3. Budget vs. Actual: Revenue → Tournaments $1,440.00 actual with no budget ("Nothing in Tournaments was budgeted for this year", + "Registration revenue — not planned"); Expenses → Tournaments $3,000 budgeted, $0 actual ("Entry Fees" — the club's own entry fees to other events). The tournament's own costs (umpires, field time, trophies) are not there.
  • My read:
    • The money is findable, but the book and the tournament do not know about each other. The tournament says "not tracked here"; the club books say $1,440 came in. A reader would conclude the tournament lost track of its own payments, or that the club's books are wrong.
    • Layout/Feedback: the book opens on an empty month under a $1,940 balance. The empty state ("Nothing on this book in this window") is true but the person has no clue the entries are earlier. This is the single most confusing screen in the journey (O5-17).
    • Effort: from inside the tournament, the only route is Club overview → Accounting → scroll → row → Date → All time. Nothing inside tournament admin links to its own book; nothing in the book links back to the tournament.
    • Hand-off: the Overview "Tournaments" card reads "Schedules, results, registrations and game day"; nothing about money. The Accounting card on Overview lists tabs, not the tournaments' books.
    • Sums: BvA Revenue → Tournaments $1,440 vs the tournament book $1,940: the $500 float is a transfer, not revenue. That is correct accounting and nowhere explained on the ledger line.
  • Findings: · High · The tournament and the club's books contradict each other on the same money: the tournament says "payments aren't tracked here" while the club book shows $1,440 of its registration revenue, and the dashboard has no door to the book. Evidence: O5-02 Payments card, O5-05 settings form, O5-20 ledger, O5-18 BvA. Direction: the Payments card should say what is in the club's book for this event (in / out / net) and link to it, and the book should link back to the event. (Walk finished only because the owner knows to look under Accounting.) · Med · The tournament's book opens on "this month" and shows an empty window under a non-zero balance. Evidence: O5-17. Direction: open a tournament's book on "All time" (or the event's own dates). · Med · Costs out for hosting a tournament have no home in the tournament's book (only the club's own entry fees to other events are budgeted). Evidence: O5-20 (nothing out), O5-18 (Expenses → Tournaments $0, "Entry Fees"). Direction: a "Hosted tournament" cost category tied to the event (the Event settings text promises "entry fees and costs filed under this category appear together in By activity" — this walk never reached a "By activity" screen). · Low · Document title on a club page carries the tournament's name ("Members - Harbourtown Invitational 2026 - Harbourtown Minor Ball …" seen on a club-level screen after a tournament visit). Evidence: page title on /admin/org/members (seen in the A5 run on this copy). Direction: club pages should not carry a tournament name in the tab title.

The journey as a whole

  • Where a first-timer gets stuck: money. The crossing in and out is fine on a computer. The owner's real question — "did the tournament make or lose money, and where is it?" — has no answer inside the tournament and a 6-click one in the club's books that opens on an empty month.
  • The hand-off between the two areas is by position, not by link: "Club overview" is the only door between them, and neither side shows the other's figures.
  • Top 3: (1) tournament and books disagree, no link (High). (2) book opens on an empty month (Med). (3) club "Tournaments" door opens one event, list hidden under ADMIN (Med).

Shape questions for the owner

  • Should a tournament's money live in the tournament's admin (a Money card that reads its book) rather than only in Accounting? — Reshape: keep the books where they are, but make the tournament's Payments card read from them and link. Rides on: whether a tournament admin who is not a club owner may see club money (a staff role without module_accounting would see a number they cannot open).
  • Should the club's "Tournaments" door open a list? — Reshape, small: when there is more than one tournament, or "New tournament" is wanted. Rides on: the 1-click direct entry that works well for one event.

Club admin · Dana Kowalski, Vice-president, operations

The admin's arrival is the cleanest of the five (four page changes from the email to a working screen), but a new club's Overview is empty for them and the owner's setup is invisible. Their two emergencies show the club's time at its weakest: a rain-out is found in three clicks on the Calendar and then done in three separate tools, and when the city takes two Saturdays back nothing anywhere says what was booked on them. Changing the board removes a person by deleting their account, and that includes a parent's family sign-in in the same club.

Keep: The Calendar as the place a rain-out is foundKeep: The invite accept page’s role sentenceKeep: Spring registration’s club notice on the public site

Five journeys, one at a time. Each station: the captures (click to open at full size, with the measurements), what the walker saw and did, their read, and the findings. A flag opens the finding; ✓ means the parent reopened the capture or the code.

A1 · First time — the club admin (vice-president) (desktop, + phone landing and More sheet)

Started at: the invite link for navj-fresh-admin@dev.local (made with inviteLink + followInvite; the real email cannot be delivered on dev) · Finished? yes — accepted, landed, explored every door the rail and the Overview offer · Effort: link → accept page (1 page) → fill 3 fields + 1 click → Overview (2.7 s). 4 page changes from the email click to a working screen, 0 guesses.

Station 1The invite email, then the accept page

  • URL: /auth/accept-invite?org=navj-fresh&role=admin&inviter=Alex+Rivera · measured: 1 screen, main action above fold: yes ("Create account and join", y=482), 46 words above fold, 5 small targets (all in the marketing header).
  • What they see and do — the email (code read, lib/email.ts orgInviteHtml; one template for every role). Subject: "You've been invited to Fresh Hollow Minor Ball on FieldLogicHQ". Heading: "You're invited". Body: "Alex Rivera invited you to join Fresh Hollow Minor Ball on FieldLogicHQ as an administrator. Click below to accept your invitation and set up your account." Button: "Accept invitation". "This link expires in 24 hours. If you weren't expecting this invitation, you can safely ignore this email." The page: marketing header (Home, Scores, Pricing, Get started ▾), title "Join Fresh Hollow Minor Ball as Admin", "Alex Rivera invited you. Set a password to finish.", the role sentence ("You'd help run the organization: every program on its plan."), First name / Last name / Password / "Create account and join".
  • My read: 1 ease good — three fields and one button; the role sentence is exactly where the question ("what am I signing up for?") arises. 5 text — the email never says what FieldLogicHQ *is*, what an administrator can do, or what to expect after the click; it spends its only descriptive words on the 24-hour expiry. A person who has never heard of the product sees a stranger's name, a brand, a role noun. 10 one name — email "administrator", page "Admin", Members table "Admin": three spellings of one role. 7 where am I — the page keeps the public marketing header (including a "Get started" menu that invites a competing signup and a "Pricing" link) above a form for joining someone else's club; the phone version has none of it and is cleaner. 11 — no "you're in" moment: the page redirects in 2.7 s with no confirmation. 12 — the 24-hour expiry is short for a volunteer who sees the email on Sunday.
  • Findings: · Med · The invite email is one generic template — it does not say what the product is, what the role opens, or what happens next · email text above · direction: add the role sentence the accept page already has ("You'd help run the organization…") and one line on what FieldLogicHQ is. · Low · One role, three names (administrator / Admin / Admin) and League admin vs "league administrator" in the email · email vs · direction: one table (it already exists: ROLE_EMAIL_LABEL) — align the page title to it or the reverse. · Low · The desktop accept page wears the public marketing header (Get started ▾, Pricing); the phone page does not · vs · direction: the focused first-run frame, as the plan door uses.

The journey as a whole

  • Where a first-timer gets stuck: nowhere — this is the smoothest of the five. The accept page is short, the landing is plain and the "Owner only" rows are honest. The weakness is emptiness without direction: an admin lands on a club with nothing in it and no list of what is theirs to start.
