  • What it says about the nav: the rail works for an admin; "Also on your plan" mislabels a program the admin runs; the locked "Owner only" rows model the right way to say "not yours".
  • Top 3: (no first-day direction), (generic email), (Help's first-day content buried and unfiltered).

Shape questions for the owner

  • Should the admin see the owner's open setup steps (read-only)? — Reshape: recommend yes; a club is set up by two people, and a "Still to do" line costs one row. Rides on: the checklist's ending (O1 ).
  • One invite email per role with the role's sentence in it? — Reshape: recommend yes; the sentence already exists on the accept page. Rides on: nothing, copy only (/marketing).
  • Existing-account "added" email (no accept step): its sign-in link goes to /auth/login?next=/navj-fresh/admin for every role — see T1 for the landing consequence. — Keep / Reshape: for an admin it is correct (Overview).

A2 · Rain-out — club admin Dana Kowalski (desktop; phone NOT walked)

Started at: the admin Overview, then Calendar in the sidebar · Finished? YES in the second pass (see below); first pass: stopped at "find every game and practice": I found them and did not get to cancel/move or notify. The cause is the rig, not the product (see Blocker). · Effort so far: setup about 55 tool steps (not judged); the find itself, 3 clicks and 1 page change from the sidebar.

Blocker (rig, not product)

Partway through, the production build that :3100 serves was wiped: .next now holds only dev (a next dev was started at 13:04, the owner's :3000, which owns that folder). HTML still comes back from the running server, but every /_next/static/* asset returns 500, so pages are unstyled and nothing is interactive. I did not rebuild (the brief forbids a build) and did not touch :3000. To resume: node .probe/p5-prodbuild.cjs build then start, ideally with no dev server running in the same folder. Every other helper on :3100 will hit the same wall.

Setup (not judged), exactly what I put on the copy

The copy has no club schedule. I used the club's own tools:

  • Permit (added in Organization > Venue library > Permits > Add permit): "Saturday diamonds, December 2026", Town of Milton, P-2026-1301, Nov 28 to Dec 19 2026, Saturdays 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m., Kinsmen Park Diamond A + B, $800 on the "Diamond permits" budget line. (The fixture's own permits have no November/December Saturdays: Fall diamonds is Tue/Thu; Summer fields 2027 starts May 3.)
  • Club schedule from the permit ("Hand out this time in a schedule" link on the permit window opens New schedule with the permit filled in): "Saturdays at Kinsmen, December 2026", a set number a week: 14U AA 1, 15U AA 1, 13U AAA 1, House league 6; saved as a draft, then Send. That Send tells coaches by email, so I unticked every coach so it read "Send to 0": the slots became real bookings and nobody was emailed. I also built an earlier "Saturdays at Kinsmen, spring 2027" the same way from the Summer fields permit (14U AA, 9U AA, House league) and gave House league's share to U9 Rookie, then generated 2 spring games (May 8, May 15, drafts).
  • House league Saturday games in the Fall season: the share goes to League admins to divide ("House league's time" > "Give it to" a division), then Tools > Generate games. U9 Rookie could not be generated because the fixture already holds a draft game on Nov 19; so I used Add Event > Game and entered three Dec 5 games by hand (U9 Reds vs Blues 10:00 a.m. Diamond A and 12:00 p.m. Diamond B; U11 Hawks vs Owls 11:00 a.m. Diamond A). A U13 game did not save (I did not retry).
  • What the copy holds on Sat Dec 5, 2026: 3 House league games (drafts, not published) and 3 rep practices (14U AA 1:00 Diamond A, 15U AA 1:00 Diamond B, 13U AAA 2:00 Diamond A), all at Kinsmen Park. Dec 12 and 19 each carry 3 rep practices.
  • Things I tripped on during setup (observations, not scored): picking a Saturday in the club wizard takes ~25 interactions; a coach is emailed by Send unless you untick them; the House league share is a second job that a league admin normally does; manual games are not tied to the club's time at all (venue is typed, "Club venue" chip appears).

Station 1Where is Saturday?

  • What they see and do: "Calendar" is the second item in the sidebar, above Programs. It opens on a List of the current week (every day "—"), with List / Week / Month, filters Venue, Program, Team, and Export. A person who wants "this Saturday" has it directly. For a Saturday weeks away: Month > next arrow > the cell reads "6 bookings"; clicking the cell drops into the List for that week, showing the 6 items in order with the program and place on each: "10:00–11:00 a.m. Reds vs Blues, House league · U9 Rookie · Kinsmen Park · Diamond A", "11:00 a.m. Hawks vs Owls, House league · U11 Pinto", "12:00 p.m. Reds vs Blues…", then "1:00 p.m. 14U AA · Practice", "1:00 p.m. 15U AA · Practice", "2:00 p.m. 13U AAA · Practice".
  • My read: Yes: one place shows the whole club's Saturday, house league and rep teams together, in time order. That is the answer to the journey's central question, and it needed no hunting by program. Program and Team filters narrow it. Where am I: heading "Calendar" with the week range; sidebar highlights Calendar. The month cell label "6 bookings" does not say whose or how many are games vs practices.
  • Findings:
    • · Med · The calendar lists House league draft games (nobody told, not published) with the same look as published ones; the admin cannot tell which of Saturday's 6 items a family already knows about. This matters in a rain-out: cancelling a draft should tell no one, cancelling a published game should. Evidence: (no marker on the three House league rows). Direction: a "Draft" tag on unpublished rows.
    • · Low · "Calendar" opens on the current week, not the next Saturday; a rain-out is usually next Saturday, one day away or a week away. Fine in production; here it cost me the month detour only because my fixture is in the future.

Station 2Cancel or move each item and tell people — NOT REACHED

I opened none of the items before the rig failed, so I have no verdict on: what an item's detail offers (cancel vs move), whether one action can cancel the whole Saturday, what a family or coach would receive, and the phone start. Do not read the absence of findings here as a pass. What I can say from the setup, which did touch these tools:

  • · Med · Telling people is split across three tools by program: a club schedule Send tells rep coaches (and says "Nothing is emailed to a family"), the House league season's "Email families" tells that season's families, and the public-site Club notice (one line, ends by itself, with a "Tonight" choice made for exactly this) tells anyone who visits. There is no single "cancel Saturday and tell everyone" action that I found. Evidence: the Send dialog (), , . This is a finding from the wiring I saw, not from walking the rain-out; confirm when the rig is back.
  • The Send dialog's wording is a good example to copy: it states the number of bookings it makes real, who is told, names each coach, shows a "See Taylor Brooks' email" preview, and offers "For review first".

The journey as a whole

  • Where a first-timer gets stuck: not seen yet (the hard part is after the find).
  • Hand-offs: the Send dialog names each coach and offers an email preview; the families are told by a different screen.
  • What this says about the nav: Calendar is a strong top-level door for "what is on", and it is the right start for a rain-out. Schedules (the club's time handed to teams) is a different thing from the calendar; the sidebar names them side by side without saying so.
  • Top 3 issues: (drafts look live), (no one place to tell everyone, unconfirmed), blocker.
  • To finish: re-walk Station 2 on navj-club-5, Sat Dec 5 2026, opening each of the 6 items; then the phone start (Calendar on a phone, cancel from the field).

Shape questions for the owner

  • Should the Calendar be where a rain-out is *done* (select a day, cancel everything, one message), not just where it is found? — Keep the Calendar as the door; reshape the follow-through — I could not confirm what is there.

The admin's version shows the same program list as plain text, with no Suspend, and says nothing about why the list is not editable. The only sentence is about plan & billing.     • Text: "permanently deletes their account" is a heavy sentence for a volunteer who is simply stepping down, and the admin has no softer door (Suspend). It does not say what stays behind (registrations the registrar approved, family emails sent). If the person is also in another club or has a Coaches Portal team, the product keeps the account and removes only the membership — the dialog is said to adapt, but this walk only met the sole-presence wording.
    • Feedback: banner after removal is plain and true. The leaver's own experience is a silent redirect to sign-in.
    • One name: "board" (page heading), "members" (route and sidebar), "club" ("removed from the club"), "organization" (the hub). Four words for one group.
  • Findings: · Med · The admin's Manage window shows access as read-only text without saying only the owner changes it, and without the Suspend option the owner has. Evidence: A5-04 vs A5-11. Direction: one line "Only the club owner can change what [name] can open or suspend them", or show the controls disabled. · Med · Remove says "permanently deletes their account" for a volunteer stepping down, with no softer option for the admin and no hint of what stays. Evidence: A5-05. Direction: say what is kept (their past work stays under their name) and put Suspend within the admin's reach, or say why not. · Low · A removed person who is mid-session lands on sign-in with no reason. Evidence: A5-07. Direction: "Your access to Harbourtown Minor Ball was removed" on that sign-in. · Low · "Board / members / club / organization" for one group. Evidence: A5-03 heading, A5-02 hub, A5-06 banner. Direction: pick one for the screen and the banner.

Station 3Invite the replacement in the right role

  • What they see and do: Invite → "Invite someone to Harbourtown Minor Ball (navj-club-4)", Email, Role defaulting to Staff with "You'd help on game day: schedules, scores and check-in." The role list is grouped: RUNS THE CLUB (Admin — every program; Treasurer — the money; Staff — game-day help), HOUSE LEAGUE (League admin — runs the house league; League registrar — league sign-ups), VOLUNTEERS (Volunteer — scores or the gate). Picking League registrar changes the helper line to "You'd look after house league registrations." Send invite is the next click (not pressed).
  • My read:
    • First-time ease: Med. The default role is Staff, the lowest-stakes, but it is the wrong default for an admin replacing a registrar and nothing forces a choice. The helper sentence is written in the second person for the invitee ("You'd help…"), which reads like the admin is being addressed.
    • Is this mine: the Admin role is offered to the admin ("every program"). An admin can make another admin. No warning on the screen.
    • Names: role titles on the invite (League registrar) and the title the leaver had ("Registrar") are separate fields; the invite cannot set a title, so the new person will read as "League registrar" with no title until someone opens Manage. The old title is lost.
    • The "Volunteer" and "Staff" rows sit one group apart with similar short lines (game-day help / scores or the gate) — two near-synonyms.
  • Findings: · Med · The role defaults to Staff and the one-line help is written to the invitee, not the admin. Evidence: A5-08 and A5-10. Direction: start on "Choose a role" and word the line for the admin ("Can open: House league registrations"). · Low · Staff vs Volunteer read as the same thing. Evidence: A5-09. Direction: describe by what they can open, not by "help".

Added in session 3: · High · Removing a club member who is also a parent in the same club’s family app deletes their account, so the parent loses their family sign-in. The keep-the-account check counts another club or a free team page, never a family account in this club. The window says "This permanently deletes their account", which an admin reads as the staff access only. Volunteers in a minor-ball club are almost always parents there.

Station 4What will the new person see before they arrive?

  • What they see and do: There is no preview or "see as". What the admin can read is a table at the foot of Members, "What each role can open": rows Rep teams, Accounting, Public site, House league · Tournaments, Families, Members, Plan & billing · Settings · Audit log; columns "On [club]'s plan", Owner, Admin, Treasurer, Staff, League admin, League registrar (and, off the right edge on a 1440 screen, Volunteer and Coach). It is sitting behind the invite window while the admin picks the role. It does not show the sidebar, the first landing or what is missing from their nav.
  • My read:
    • Layout / where: good that it is on the same page; but it is under the fold (page 1.34 screens) and not linked from the invite window. The role list inside the window is the only thing the admin reads at the moment of choosing.
    • The table's "Admin" column says ✓ for the admin on Rep teams, Accounting, Public site, House league·Tournaments, Members, but the admin's own board line says "Every program on the plan" while Families is "if you turn it on" (and this admin cannot turn it on). So "every program" overstates by one.
    • Hand-off: nothing says what the new person will land on or that an invitation link lasts a certain time. The only time-bound text I saw was on the coach invite ("a link that works for 7 days"), not here.
    • The people table's "What they can open" column, one line per person ("House league registrations"), is the best preview of a role the admin gets, and it only exists for people already on the board.
  • Findings: · Med · No preview of what an invited role will see; the one table that answers it is below the fold, truncated at the right on 1440 px, and not linked from the invite window. Evidence: A5-03, A5-10. Direction: a "What this role can open" line (or the first landing, as a small picture) under the role picker, plus a link to the full table. · Low · "Every program on the plan" is worded as complete for an admin who cannot open Families. Evidence: A5-03 admin row vs the matrix. Direction: "Every program except Families" or add the toggle's state.

Station 5What the admin cannot do, and how that shows

  • What they see and do: If the admin types the owner-only addresses: Plan & billing → "Billing access required — Only [club]'s owner can see and change the plan and how it's paid" (full page, in frame); Settings → "Settings are the owner's" (and a 403 in the console); Audit log → a bare 404 "We can't find that page".
  • My read: three different answers to the same situation (a polite page, a polite page, a 404). Only an admin who types addresses sees them; the sidebar already hides all three.
  • Findings: · Low · Owner-only pages answer with three different messages, one a 404. Evidence: A5-13/14/15. Direction: one "owner's only" page.

The journey as a whole

  • Where a first-timer gets stuck: not in the clicks (Members is where a person would look; removal and invite are two short windows) but in not knowing what is theirs to do. The admin finds the owner-only list on Overview, then discovers the owner-only parts of Manage only by comparing with the owner's view.
  • The hand-off: the new person's first arrival was walked by the registrar's first-time journey (R1), not here. From the admin's side nothing tells them what the new person sees, and the leaver is dropped without a word.
  • Top 3: (1) no preview of what a role sees (Med). (2) owner-only parts of Manage not explained, Suspend invisible (Med). (3) "permanently deletes their account" with no softer path (Med).

Shape questions for the owner

  • Should an admin be able to suspend as well as remove? — Reshape: Remove deletes the person's account when they are sole-presence, which is final; for a volunteer leaving, suspend is the safer first step. Rides on the owner's ruling that capabilities and suspension stay owner-only (members route comments).
  • Should the invite show what the role will open (and the first screen they land on)? — Keep the table, add a one-line summary beside the role picker. Rides on nothing structural; a small build.
  • Should a new admin be inviteable by an admin? — Not yet: leave as is, but the dialog should say it. Rides on the board's trust model.

League admin · Jules Moreau, House league convener

The league admin's whole job is house league, and the product treats their program as an extra until a season exists ("Also on your plan" on a computer, absent from the phone bar). Their schedule depends on the club's time, and that hand-off fails both ways: when time is given they are not told and the season says the opposite; when it isn't, the screen points them at a page they can't open and gives them nobody to ask. Inside the season the work is good: forming teams, the publish window's email preview, and next year's roll-over are among the best screens walked.

Keep: The publish window’s inline email preview (L3)Keep: The roll-over window ("Start next season from this one")Keep: The Practice time dialogKeep: The house league coach’s team page

Five journeys, one at a time. Each station: the captures (click to open at full size, with the measurements), what the walker saw and did, their read, and the findings. A flag opens the finding; ✓ means the parent reopened the capture or the code.

Registrar · Riley Okonkwo, House league registrar

The registrar does the most family-facing work and gets the least help with it. Their first landing tells them to create a season they can't create. Their desk works for the easy cases (approve, mark a cheque received), but the common hard ones have no path: a likely duplicate's only exits email the family, there is no fee reminder, and a part refund takes two operations in the right order. On the phone, "which team is she on" is answered on the row, one tab away from where search looks.

Keep: Decline’s "Decline and email" label and its note boxKeep: Mark received (4 clicks, method recorded)Keep: The answer on the row: "U9 Rookie · Reds"

Waitlist in the same bar asks the same way ("Each family is emailed that their child is on the waitlist.").
  • My read: 2 flow: the two Approves behave differently. The bulk press tells you who is emailed and the single press, which sends the same email, says nothing. 5 text: the confirm names the email's content but doesn't show it. 4 layout: the bulk bar sits above the table, not pinned. Ticking Ruby near the bottom of the list leaves the bar off-screen ( shows two ticks and no bar, because the page was scrolled), so the next move is a hunt. 9 dead ends: none, but the over-full U9 let me approve a ninth child into an eight-child division. U9 Active is now 9 against a cap of 8, and the product said nothing. The approve counts a child who already held a spot as free, which the settings line "A child waiting for review holds a spot" implies, but the registrar is not told. 11 feedback: toast is brief and sits over a control.
  • Findings: · Med · Single-row Approve emails the family with no confirm and no words about it, while the bulk path confirms and names the email; one slip sends an email · vs · direction: the same sentence on the row hint, or confirm both. · Med · The bulk bar isn't pinned: ticking a lower row scrolls it out of view · · direction: sticky bar. · Med · Approving into an over-full division succeeds quietly (U9 now 9 of 8). The product's "full" refusal only guards children coming off the waitlist, and nothing names the difference · /registrations?tab=active U9 · direction: warn on approve when the division is at or over its cap.

Station 3The duplicate (Ruby Castellano) and the Alvarez siblings

  • What they see and do: two rows, "Ruby Castellano · Signed up Nov 5" and "… Nov 2", same guardian, same email, same division, side by side in the queue. Nothing marks them as a pair, and the record window shows no birth date. Its actions are Approve, Send a new link, Decline ("emails the family"), Email this family, Waitlist ("emails the family"). The only way to settle it without writing to the family is to Decline, which opens "Decline Ruby Castellano? The family is emailed." with an optional note and "Decline and email". The Alvarez siblings are two unrelated-looking rows: Mateo (U9, active, paid) and Sofia (U11, to review). The registrar sees no household link. Searching "Alvarez" in To review shows only Sofia.
  • My read: 2 flow wrong for a registrar: the duplicate queue lives in Families (a tool the registrar does not have), and the registrations screen does not mention it. 8 mine/missing: the one tool that detects likely duplicates is not theirs. 5 text: declining a duplicate emails a "not accepted" notice to a family whose other sign-up they will accept, which is the wrong message. A quiet "Remove this duplicate" would not tell them anything. 13 hand-off: no way to ask the duplicates owner to merge.
  • Findings: · High · A likely-duplicate pair looks like two ordinary sign-ups, and the only exits are Approve (I did not press it on a Ruby; the code refuses a second active record) or Decline, which emails the family "not accepted" about a child they are already accepted for · , · direction: flag the pair on the row and offer a no-email "Same child, remove". · Med · Ruby's record window has no Date of birth row at all, so "this one has no birth date" (the clue that tells the two sign-ups apart) is a silent absence, not a flag; an accepted child's record does show it (Zoe, R4) · · direction: show "Date of birth: not given" on the row. I did not open the second Ruby. · Low · Siblings across divisions are not linked in the list (no household chip) so the registrar cannot answer "one email or two?" before approving.

Station 4Waitlist and decline (stopped)

  • What they see and do: Waitlist via the bar: "Move 2 children to the waitlist? Each family is emailed that their child is on the waitlist." The Waitlist tab lists #1–#3 with a "Promote" button each. Stopped here: the family email. The Decline window's only preview of what the family reads is one line plus an optional note. The email's wording itself is not shown here, unlike Email families, which has "See the email". Promote on a full division was not pressed.
  • My read: 5 text: both windows promise an email but neither shows it. 12 effort: decline = menu, item, optional note, button, 4 clicks. "The spot stays open. You move the waitlist up yourself." is a good line and where it matters.
  • Findings: · Low · Decline and Waitlist emails can't be previewed (Email families can) · · direction: reuse "See the email".

The journey as a whole

  • Where a first-timer gets stuck: knowing what to do with the duplicate pair and with an over-full U9. After each approve the registrar sees a toast and a shorter list (good), but not what the family now has to do, or that a fee of $150 is now owing (visible only on Active).
  • Hand-offs: approve → family gets an email with the fee and how to pay → fee shows as "owing" on Active (R3). The registrar never sees that email.
  • Top 3: duplicate pair (High); + approve is unconfirmed and silently over-fills; the bulk bar isn't pinned.

Shape questions for the owner

  • Should the likely-duplicate flag reach the registrar (it sits in Families)? — Reshape: the one person who meets duplicates first can't see or fix them. Rides on the registrar's role grant.
  • Does Approve into a full division mean "over-fill on purpose" or a bug? — Reshape: decide, then say it on the screen.

But the filter is hidden behind a button, so a first-timer scrolls the Active list hunting for amber. 8 mine: right. 7 where am I: the active filter is shown as a chip and the Filter button carries a "1".

Stopped before Send. It reads "This season can send 3 emails in any 24 hours."

The registrar writes one message for 12 families that can't say what each one owes ($75 vs $175). 10 one name: the bar's "Email" and the sidebar's "Email families" are the same tool. The page itself is empty-state-first ("No emails to this season's families yet"). 13 hand-off: the family receives a generic email, not a statement. The cap of 3 per 24 hours is shown only inside the window.

The journey as a whole

You move the waitlist up yourself." talks about the division's spot, not the team's.

The journey as a whole

Treasurer · Avery Chen, Treasurer

The treasurer's landing is right (Accounting, not the club Overview) and the coach's expense claim is the strongest hand-off in the product: a bell, a This morning tile and a badge, then approve and pay in one step. The weak side is everything that starts with someone else: the owner's dome split is on a screen the treasurer can't open, and nothing stops the same teams being billed twice. House league money is readable but has no door, and the figures don't open their lines.

Keep: Landing on AccountingKeep: The coach claim’s arrival: bell + tile + badge, approve-and-pay in one stepKeep: The close-year screenKeep: The Accounting Overview’s "Where the club stands" (the best summary screen walked)

Five journeys, one at a time. Each station: the captures (click to open at full size, with the measurements), what the walker saw and did, their read, and the findings. A flag opens the finding; ✓ means the parent reopened the capture or the code.

Typed /calendar → "Nothing to show — The calendar shows the programs you can open, and your role opens none of them." Help → /help/accounting from the rail is right for them; the Help hub (/help) is the same 9 cards every role sees, Tournaments (26 topics) first.

The journey as a whole

T2 · The dome bill, the money side — Treasurer (desktop)

Started at: the treasurer's landing /navj-club-2/admin/accounting (navj-club-2-treasurer), as a treasurer who has heard "the owner is setting up the dome" and wants the dome cost, each team's share, installments, who has paid and who is late · Finished? With help, and partly no. The treasurer can see the dome's COST and its budget line, and can read the overdue-installments and reminder screens (stopped before "Send 5 reminders"), but cannot see the owner's per-team split at all (it lives on a screen the treasurer does not have), and there is no dome bill to see until the owner finalizes. The treasurer's only way to bill the dome is to build their own allocation by hand · Effort: about 5 clicks to the allocation list, 7 to the New allocation window, 3 to the reminder preview; the permit via Organization > Venue library > Permits is 4 more.

The copy's dome state at the time of this walk: the owner's schedule exists as a DRAFT with the bill added (3 payments), NOT finalized and NOT sent (hard stop), so Accounting holds no dome bill yet. The treasurer therefore sees the world a real treasurer would see in the days between "the owner built it" and "the owner finalized it".

Station 1The treasurer's landing: where do I see the dome?

  • What they see and do: the sidebar has Overview, Accounting (3), Organization and nothing else (no Calendar, no Schedules, no Rep teams: correct for a treasurer). Accounting opens on "Where the club stands - today, Nov 6": Cash on hand $2,870, Owed by the teams $10,950 ("$3,450.00 overdue · $450.00 sent, waiting for you"), Waiting on you $920 (3 requests). Below: "From 2025-26, still open" (3 rows, $1,460), "2026-27 against the budget" (Revenue $16,550 planned, Expenses $46,000, Net -$29,450), "The teams: 8 teams · 5 teams have money late", the club's four books. Nothing says "dome"; the winter dome is only inside the planned expenses.
  • My read: First-time ease: the overall picture is good, and overdue is the loudest figure, which is right for a treasurer. Does it show the dome? No. Is this mine: yes. Where am I: clear.
  • Findings: · Low · no sign anywhere on the landing that a $27,000 dome has been rented or that the owner has a bill waiting on a draft schedule · T2-01 · direction: owner's call; a quiet "Dome time: $27,000 planned, not yet billed to teams" row on Budget vs. Actual would answer it.

Station 2The dome's cost: Budget

  • What they see and do: Budget is a grouped list. Under Expenses > Facilities: "Diamond permits - city fields $9,000 planned, $8,550 allocated, $1,800 collected" and "Dome time - winter dome · No date yet · $27,000.00" with ALLOCATED, COLLECTED and OPEN blank. So the dome's cost is found in two clicks (Accounting then Budget), and the empty allocated column is the honest answer: the money is not yet billed to anyone. Revenue "From the teams" says $11,550 from 3 allocations: that line does not include the dome. The closing balance is therefore -$29,115 until the dome is billed.
  • My read: Does the treasurer find the owner's split? Not here. The budget line tells the treasurer how much the dome costs but not that the owner has a split drawn; "No date yet" is the weakest word on the page, because the treasurer is the person who must find the cash to pay the dome and the permit has no payment dates either (see O2 ).
  • Findings: · Med · the "Dome time" budget line has "No date yet" and no owed-to-the-dome schedule; the treasurer cannot see when the CLUB pays the dome · T2-02 · direction: the same "how we pay for it" fields as O2 feed this column.

Station 3The permit, read as a treasurer

  • What they see and do: the treasurer CAN open the permit (read only: no pencil, no renew, no delete, no "Hand out this time"). It shows the same cost block ($27,000.00, $72/hour full field, half fields at $36), the budget line ("Dome time - winter dome · 2026-27 · Open the line >") and the use bar (0 of 450 h), plus the sentence '"Winter dome 2026-27" hands this time out, so the permit stays.' The sentence is plain text; the treasurer has no Schedules door and no link to the schedule or its bill.

  • Findings: · Med · the treasurer is told a schedule hands the permit out but can reach neither the schedule nor its "Fair shares", so the owner's split is invisible to the person who will chase the money · T2-10 · direction: a read-only Fair shares view (or the proposed bill) for the treasurer on the Allocations page, or a link from the permit.

Station 4Each team's share and the installments (the treasurer's way)

  • What they see and do: Accounting > Teams is a table with each team's Allocated / Collected / Outstanding / overdue / cash on hand. Allocations lists four allocations (Permit share 2025-26, Fall ball diamond fees 2026, Umpire fees 2026, Diamond fees 2026 with 5 teams and 5 OVERDUE). There is no dome allocation, because the owner's bill is sitting on the draft schedule and has not been written to Accounting. The treasurer who wants the dome billed would click "New allocation": Bill from (a list that includes "Dome time - winter dome · $27,000.00 left"), Name, Amount, Split: Evenly / By amount / By percentage / By sessions, Pay by (One payment, 2 to 10 installments), a per-team list. The owner's split is "by the time each team got", with half fields counted half, priced at the permit's rates. The treasurer's Split options do not offer that, so building the same split means typing 7 dollar amounts from a number they cannot see. Evenly would be $3,857.14 each, versus the owner's $3,708 to $3,960. The dome line says "$27,000.00 left" even though the owner has already put a $27,000 bill on a draft, so nothing stops the two people billing the dome twice.
  • My read: Does the treasurer find the owner's split, or have to build it? Has to build it (or wait for finalize). Do the two views agree? Not yet: the owner's schedule says "the bill: $27,000 in 3 payments (Oct 1, Dec 1, Feb 1)"; Accounting says Dome time has $27,000.00 left and nothing allocated. After finalize they should agree (the owner's dialog says "each team's share arrives on its Money > Club tab with its 3 payments, filed under Dome Time") - not verified, because finalize also sends.

  • What they see and do: an allocation opens as a window: Allocated / Collected / Outstanding / Overdue, "Schedule: One installment: Dec 6", then a table of TEAM, HEAD COACH, COLLECTED, OUTSTANDING, NEXT, STATE with groups "ON TRACK · 2" and (for the other allocations) "OVERDUE". There is a Previous / Next walker across allocations. Overdue, paid and "sent, waiting for you" are all present. For the dome there is no such row yet (see Station 4).

  • What they see and do: "Send reminders - Remind about: Overdue, and due in the next 14 days". WHO GETS ONE · 5 TEAMS with each coach and each line ("Diamond fees 2026, 1 of 3 · $450.00 · 45 days late - and ..."), then "Nobody to send to · 1 team: 12U AA has no head coach, so its reminder (...) can't go. Once you've sent the money, open Money > Club in your team's portal and tap We've sent it". Buttons: Cancel, "Send 5 reminders" (not pressed).

The journey as a whole

  • Does the treasurer find the owner's split or have to build it? They have to build it, or wait until the owner finalizes. Before finalize, Accounting and the schedule disagree: the schedule says the dome is billed (in draft); Accounting says $27,000.00 left. After finalize they should agree (unverified).

  • What it says about the nav: money is split across two roles with two doors: the owner bills teams from a schedule view (Fair shares), the treasurer bills teams from Allocations. Both write the same kind of thing (a dated installment per team) but they have different splits, different defaults and no shared view of "this dome is being billed".

Shape questions for the owner

  • Should a draft bill on a schedule reserve the permit's budget line, so Accounting shows "being billed: $27,000 (draft)" until finalized? — Reshape - recommend yes; riding on it: a double-billed dome, or a treasurer who does not know the money is coming.
  • Should the treasurer see the schedule's Fair shares, read-only? — Keep or reshape - recommend yes (read only), since they chase the money.
  • Should the dome be billed from the schedule only (the owner's route), with Accounting's "New allocation" refusing the dome line? — Not yet - recommend deciding with the owner and treasurer who owns the dome bill; riding on it: two doors to one bill.

Started at: coach navj-club-7-coach-15aaa lands on the 15U AAA team Overview in the Coaches Portal. · Finished? yes, end to end, no help. · Effort: coach: Money → Club tab → Make a request → 2 dropdown picks → search a category → 3 fields → Submit = 3 page/tab changes, about 10 actions.   • What they see and do: the row opens a window: the coach's quote, Direction, For, "Filed by the coach as: Money back for a cost", "In the team's budget: Team Gear › Helmets", "Asked by Jordan Reyes · Nov 6", "How they'd like it: Card", with Decline and Approve. T5 · Year end for the board — treasurer Avery Chen, `navj-club-7-treasurer` (desktop; phone look at Budget vs. Actual)

Started at: Accounting Overview (the treasurer's landing) · Finished? with help. The fixture's only closable year (2025–26) had already been closed by the seed, so I used the product's own Reopen (with a reason) to reach the close screen, then closed it again. The current year (2026–27) cannot be closed before it ends on Aug 31 (the Close door only appears the day after a year ends). I changed data on my copy only. · Effort: to read the year: 1 click (Budget vs. Actual) or 0 (Overview). To hand it over: Export → PDF/Excel/CSV, 2 clicks. To close: pill → year → "Close 2025–26" → confirm = 4 clicks.

Station 1"How did the year go?"

  • What they see: two places answer it. The Overview ("2026–27 against the budget", a 6-line summary + books + teams) and Budget vs. Actual (the full statement: Revenue → From the teams, House league registration fees, Tournaments, Sponsorship; Expenses by category; Net). The year pill offers 2025–26 🔒, 2026–27 ●, 2027–28.
  • My read: Is there one place? Budget vs. Actual is the one place, and it does split what came in the way the task asks (rep dues = "From the teams" $2,750, house league = $2,355, tournament = $1,440), with per-season lines on expand. But the Overview summary omits the house-league and tournament lines (), and the Overview's "Owed by the teams" counts team money only: the house league's $1,740 still owing from 12 players is not in Accounting at all (it lives on the season's own Money page, Station 4). Where am I — the year pill is clear and shows the lock on a closed year; "To Nov 6" labels on the tables help.
  • · Med · What families still owe the house league ($1,740, 12 players) appears nowhere in Accounting; "Owed by the teams" and the Overview read as the club's whole receivable. · , · direction: a house-league line in "Owed", linking to the season's Money page.

Station 2A form to hand the board

  • What they see: "Export" on each tab: Excel (.xlsx), CSV, PDF report. Two different "PDF report"s exist: on Budget vs. Actual it is a plain 3-page table; on the Overview of a closed year it is the real board document, "The year against its budget / The year at a glance / The teams' standing with the club" (3 pages: budget table, opening → revenue → expenses → closing balance with each book, billed/collected/still owed per team, and what carries into the next year). The close screen itself tells the treasurer "Close it to lock its books before you print its year-end report."
  • My read: The year-end report is good and board-readable, and its filename ("…year-end-report-2025-26-…") says what it is. But the Budget vs. Actual PDF is not: page 1 shows bare numbers (11550, 3262.4, -1412.4), with no $ or thousands separators, spills over three pages, and prints the on-screen footnotes including "Good news is always green." On the Overview of the current year the same Export gives a year-end-style report only once the year is closed (I did not export the open-year Overview report).
  • · Med · Budget vs. Actual's PDF is not board-ready (unformatted figures, screen footnotes, 3 pages) while a polished report exists one tab over; two things are both called "PDF report". · shots/dl/T5-bva.pdf vs T5-overview-2025.pdf · direction: one report, one name; format the figures.
  • · Low · The Budget vs. Actual CSV is a summary (category totals), not transactions; I did not open the Ledger's Export, so the accountant's "every line" file is untested. · shots/dl/T5-bva.csv.

Station 3Close the fiscal year (what does it do, and is that clear before pressing it?)

  • What they see: after the year ends, the Overview carries "2025–26 ended on Aug 31 and is still open. Close it to lock its books before you print its year-end report." + an outlined Close 2025–26. The question: LOCKS (2025–26, Sep 1, 2025 to Aug 31, 2026 · 4 books, 10 lines, and its plan) → CLOSING BALANCE $335.00 "Same as last close" → CARRIES INTO 2026–27 "as its opening balance, locked". Then STILL OPEN, "None of these stop the close": 2 installments owed ($1,200), 1 line not filed ($185), 1 line not cleared ($420), each a door. A promise line: "Nothing is deleted, and you can reopen it while it is the latest closed year. Closing the club's year never touches a team's own book." Buttons "Not yet" and "Close 2025–26". After: "2025–26 is closed. 2026–27 opens on $335.00, locked."
  • My read: Is it clear before pressing? Yes: this is the clearest destructive-action screen I saw in the club walks: the outcome first (path of lock → balance → next year), what is still open counted and linked, the way back stated. Warns, never blocks. Discoverability — the door is on the Overview only, only after the year ends; a treasurer who wants to "close the year" in June will not find a pre-close and nothing says why. Nothing in the Budget tools (Fiscal year, Categories, Words your teams use) closes a year. Feedback — after Reopen, the screen briefly showed both "2025–26 is closed… Reopen" and "2025–26 is open again" until I reloaded.
  • · Low · The Close door appears only after the year ends; before that, nothing explains when it will. · · direction: one line on the Overview ("2026–27 can be closed after Aug 31").
  • · Low · Stale "closed" banner shown next to the "open again" confirmation until reload. · .
  • · Low · "Closing balance $335.00" and the Overview's live "Cash on hand $2,072.00" sit on the same page for the closed year with no word that one is as at Aug 31 and the other today (the header does say "TODAY, NOV 6"). · .

The journey as a whole

  • Finished with help (the fixture). Treasurer gets a strong close screen and a good report for a closed year, but the "how did the year go" answer is split (Overview summary vs. Budget vs. Actual vs. per-season Money pages), and the one document called "PDF report" on Budget vs. Actual is the weaker one.

The nav · walked as all five people, desktop and phone

It balances the five better than expected: four of five land on their own work, the sidebar shrinks to what each person opens, and the phone bar fills with the next door they can open. Where it fails is at the edges the sidebar doesn’t police: the Organization hub’s tiles, silent redirects, locked rows and the two "Public site" words. Those are one failure repeated: a surface that lists doors by plan, not by person. Fix those before regrouping any heading.

NAV · The club side's navigation, walked as five people (desktop 1440 + phone 390)

Fixture: navj-club (read-only, no data changed). Server: local production build on :3100. People: navj-club-owner, -admin, -leagueadmin, -registrar, -treasurer; navj-club-coach-15aaa for the Coaches Portal side of the door. Shots are in .probe/nav-journeys/shots/ (NAV-<person>-d-… desktop, -p-… phone, -x-… pages they cannot open, NAV-owner-c-… crossings, pilot-* reused). Per-shot measurements are in the .json beside each PNG and in shots/nav-log.jsonl; the words of every refusal are in shots/nav-words.out.

I could not reset it (the club is read-only), so the admin's sidebar and More sheet show Families and a Families tile. A real admin's nav, per the census, has Public site as the third tile instead. I did not see that live.
  • Every account has one workspace, so the Workspaces pill never appears (zero of five). Nobody here has a coach assignment, so the "Coaches Portal" foot door, the "You also coach" Overview row and the org hub's "My Coaches Portal" tile never appear. No cancelled club and no club without a running season exist (so "Also on your plan" never draws).

8 · One nav, five jobs

It balances them better than I expected. Four of five get a landing page that is their work (Overview "This morning" for owner/admin; Seasons for the league roles; Accounting for the treasurer), the sidebar shrinks to what the role opens, and a phone bar fills with the next door they can open. Where it fails is at the edges the sidebar does not police: the org hub's tiles, the silent redirects, the locked rows, and the two "Public site" words. Those are the same failure repeated: a surface that lists doors by plan, not by person. I would fix those before regrouping headings.

Same words, two destinations for owners; the same destination twice for everyone else; one-way trip out of the admin on a bare icon. *Recommend:* name the pill by what it does ("View site"), drop the foot door wherever the pill exists, give the live site's building icon a label. 6. Standing back · the rules that cut across the stations

Three things the evidence says that the brief didn’t ask

  1. The sidebar is not the problem, and regrouping it is the wrong first move. The nav walk found that four of five people land on their own work and the sidebar shrinks to what each opens. Every High in the nav sits at an edge the sidebar doesn't police. Recommendation: leave the groups alone ("PROGRAMS" over Accounting and Families is imperfect, but nobody got lost), and spend Stage 13 on the edges, the hand-offs and the club's time. Amended 2026-11-06, after you found the sidebar clunky: the walk judged who sees which rows, not how moving around feels. A review of that found the sidebar's shape is a problem of its own (a click you can't predict, a tree that outgrows the screen), so it is now stage 13i (Ask 25). The order holds: the edges first (13a), then the shape.
  2. Stage 13 was named "navigation across the three portals". The crossings themselves work: one click into a tournament and one back on a computer, the coach's arrival in the Coaches Portal is the best hand-off walked. What costs people is crossing between people, not portals. That is why the ladder's middle stages are about the club's time and the hand-offs.
  3. The president's view is mostly surfacing. The Accounting Overview, the Calendar, the Families filter counts and the permit windows already answer most of the owner's ten questions one click below the Overview. The Overview just doesn't point at them, including each team's standing with the club on Accounting › Teams. A band on the Overview is a Stage 13 job; the rest (free time across permits, players year over year, a board one-pager, and each team's tournaments if you say yes) is product work for the summary-layer plan you decided today, which follows the Club release.

1The hand-offs between people are the weakest part 13d

Every journey that crosses from one person to another loses the thread at the crossing. The club gives house league its time and the league admin is told nothing, while their season says the opposite. With no time given, the league admin is pointed at a page they can't open and has nobody to ask. The owner's dome split sits where the treasurer can't see it, and nothing joins the schedule's bill to the treasurer's. A club's tournament and the club's book don't link either way. A coach's "I paid by card, please e-transfer me" arrives as "How they'd like it: Card".

CopyThe coach’s expense claim reaching the treasurer (a bell, a This morning tile, a badge on Accounting, then approve and pay in one step), the rep coach’s arrival in the Coaches Portal, and the house league coach’s team page.

The ruleWhen one person’s work becomes another’s, the other side is told where they already look (the bell, a tile on their home, a badge on the row), the words say what is waiting for them, and the notice opens the step.

2Doors are listed by plan, not by person, wherever the sidebar doesn’t police 13a

The sidebar gets it right: it shrinks to what each person opens. Every other surface lists what the club's plan holds. The Organization hub's Tournaments tile takes a registrar into a tournament admin of blank and failing pages; its Members tile refuses them. Locked "Owner only" rows sit in sections that hold nothing else. The league admin's own program is "Also on your plan". Empty states are written to the owner ("Create one to get started"). And when a door isn't yours, the product answers in four different ways: a silent return to Overview, a refusal naming the owner, "You don't have access to this page", or "Nothing to show".

CopyThe sidebar itself, and the phone bar filling its slots with the next door the person can open.

The ruleOne list of doors per person, used by every surface (sidebar, phone bar, hub, Overview, empty states). One screen for "not yours": it names the page, who can open it by name, and the way back to your own home.

3The club’s time is cut into corners 13c

Permits, the thing every schedule is made from, live under Organization › Venue library behind a switch (the owner's own opinion, confirmed by O1, O2, A4 and O6). From the permit there is one good link forward ("Hand out this time in a schedule") and nothing back. The bill hides under View. The season schedule's main jobs hide in Tools. Gates are hidden instead of shown (U9 missing from Generate games, Publish absent until teams are published). A rain-out is three tools, and the Calendar that finds the Saturday can't act on it. When a permit loses two dates, nothing anywhere says six bookings sit on them. The blank schedule's default hands out a tenth of the dome.

CopyPermit → schedule pre-fill, the permit window’s Held · Booked · Unused, the Practice time dialog, and the schedule’s Needs attention box.

The ruleThe club’s time is one path a person can see: Permit → Schedule → Fair shares and the bill → Send. Every surface that shows a booking opens its home, and a change at one end tells the other.

4Numbers that don’t lead to their lines 13e

"Who owes" is answered in three unlinked places (the season's Money, Registrations' Owing filter, Families), with two different counts. Money's Still owing list is read-only. Budget vs. Actual's Not filed and Off-plan have no door to the lines behind them. One team shows two outstanding totals on two screens with nothing saying one includes last year. House league money owed is missing from the club's financial summary. The bank's "Off by" now has its Find (BC3a).

CopyAccounting Overview’s "Where the club stands", where every number reads as a sentence.

The ruleEvery figure opens the lines behind it, and a figure shown on two screens has one definition, or says which it is ("includes 2025–26").

5Actions that reach a family don’t all say so 13f

Decline says "Decline and email" and shows the note box; single-row Approve emails the family with no word and no confirm, while bulk Approve confirms and names the email. Withdraw says it in the window but not on the button. A likely duplicate's only exits email the family. Decline and Waitlist emails can't be previewed. Two product gaps sit under this: no fee reminder for families paying by cheque or e-transfer, and no part refund.

CopyThe publish window’s inline email preview (L3) and Decline’s button label.

The ruleA button that emails a family says so on the button and offers "See the email" before it sends, the same on every row and in bulk.

6One name per thing (rule 10) 13h

"Public site" is two destinations on one screen for an owner and the same destination twice for everyone else. "Tournaments" opens one event for the owner and a list inside it. The phone says Messages where the computer says Communications. Coaches and Assistant coaches sit side by side with different jobs. One act of billing has three verbs. Two different exports are both "PDF report". One role has three names between the email and the screen. House league and club pages carry a tournament's name in the browser tab.

Copy"Club overview" names the way back from a tournament the same on a computer and a phone.

The ruleOne word per door, task and idea on every surface, settled last, once the reshapes have moved things.

7The first day 13b

The setup checklist never lets the owner go (a defect: it reappears at every sign-in). The invite email is one template for every role and never says what the role opens; the accept page does. The invite form defaults to Staff even when the checklist asked for an admin. Nobody can see what a role will see before inviting. Help is filtered by plan, not by role. The "added" email's link lands every role on Overview, while every later sign-in lands them on their own home.

CopyThe checklist’s content and order (board → teams → coaches → site → budget), and the accept page’s role sentence.

The ruleEvery arrival path ends on the person’s own home, and every invitation says what the role will open.

8The phone 13g

The house league season on a phone stacks three headers before the first number (about 240 px of 844), shows the season's name three times and its state twice, and its pill strip runs off the edge so the whole page drags sideways by 63 px. A tournament is two taps in and two taps back. The phone header never says which club. The rest of the phone is clean, and the Accounting Overview reads best on a phone of any screen walked.

CopyThe phone bar’s next-door logic and the Accounting Overview on a phone.

The ruleOne header per screen on a phone; a strip that scrolls never drags the page.

13i · The sidebar’s shape, added after the walk

You found the side navigation clunky. The walk judged who sees which rows, not how moving around feels, so a review of that ran on 2026-11-06 against the code and the walk’s captures. The cause is one thing: a program’s pages are handled three different ways, so a click can’t be predicted, and the main way grows the sidebar into a deep tree that repeats the page’s own navigation. The double highlight is a plain defect and joins the fix-now list; the rest is a shape question for Ask 25, drawn in its own session before anything is built.

SeverityWhat a person meets

HighInside a house league season, "Seasons" and the page you are on are both highlighted (fix now).
HighOrganization is reachable six ways, and its sidebar rows and its tile hub disagree: Members is two clicks through a hub, and the hub holds tiles the rows don’t.
